briefing: Research this week reinforces two converging design principles for advanced carbon and 2D materials: performance gains are strongly dependent on narrow, optimized loadings and deliberate structural control. Graphene and MXene additives improved mechanical, electrical, thermal, separation and electromagnetic functions at low concentrations, whereas agglomeration or added transport resistance eroded benefits beyond optima. Architectures including aligned fibres, heterostructures and tunable metasurfaces further indicate that interfaces and orientation can convert multifunctionality into application-specific performance. Findings remain predominantly laboratory-stage.

articles.title_original: 2D MXene Nanosheet-Stabilized CaO for Enhanced Cyclic CO2 Capture and Energy-Efficient Calcium Looping
articles.title_en: MXene-Modified CaO Improves Cyclic CO2 Capture and Regeneration
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract CO2 capture using multi-cycle carbonation-calcination in calcium looping (CaL) is a promising strategy for reducing industrial carbon emissions; however, it suffers from rapid deterioration in CaO sorption capacity due to sintering and high energy requirements for regeneration. In this study, 2D-MXene nanosheet-modified CaO is proposed to enhance cyclic sorption performance and thermochemical behavior. 2D-MXene nanosheets (0.25−5 wt %) were incorporated using a simple dry-mixing approach to modify the CaO structure and evaluate its effect on cyclic stability. Structural and morphological analysis indicates that 2D-MXene incorporation is associated with reduced CaO crystallite size, improved preservation of textural characteristics, and higher accessible surface area, which are consistent with improved effective carbonation kinetics under the investigated conditions. The 1 wt % 2D-MXene-modified CaO (Ca-MX1) exhibits the best CO2 sorption performance, achieving ∼8.5 mol kg−1 in the first cycle and ∼4.9 mol kg−1 after 10 cycles at 650 °C, which is 69% higher than pure micron-sized CaO (m-CaO,∼2.9 mol kg−1). Thermochemical analysis shows that calcination and carbonation enthalpies follow sorption behavior, with m-CaO exhibiting a rapid decline in sorption capacity due to structural degradation, while the 2D-MXene-modified sample retains higher values over cycles. At comparable CO2 sorption capacities, Ca-MX1 exhibits approximately 20% lower normalized calcination enthalpy than m-CaO, indicating improved regeneration behavior at the material level under the investigated conditions. Kinetic analysis using the SCM and RPM indicates higher fitted reaction-rate and effective−diffusivity parameters for Ca-MX1, consistent with a greater contribution of reaction-controlle
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers report that 1 wt% MXene-modified CaO retained 4.9 mol kg−1 CO2 capacity after 10 cycles, 69% above pure micron-sized CaO. The composite also showed approximately 20% lower normalized calcination enthalpy at comparable capacity, indicating more energy-efficient regeneration under the tested conditions.

articles.title_original: Deformation‐Induced Electrochemical Performance of <scp> Mo <sub>2</sub> C MXene </scp> ‐Natural Rubber Flexible Supercapacitor
articles.title_en: Deformation Effects in Mo₂C MXene–Rubber Flexible Supercapacitors
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT In this work, we investigate a symmetric Mo 2 C MXene//natural rubber//Mo 2 C MXene flexible supercapacitor using a coupled electrochemical‐mechanical finite‐element framework in COMSOL Multiphysics, combining secondary current distribution, Nernst‐Planck ion transport, and Butler‐Volmer kinetics with a hyperelastic structural model. In this device, the electrode is made of Mo 2 C MXene and natural rubber as separator, maintaining mechanical flexibility and electrochemical stability. The natural rubber separator is impregnated with 1 M KOH electrolyte and the device's 0–0.6 V working potential window was established from a three‐electrode simulation of the Mo 2 C MXene electrode with reference to Ag/AgCl in 1 M KOH. The electrochemical performance is simulated under both bending and non‐bending conditions. At 1 A g −1 , the device delivers a specific capacitance of 12.50 F g −1 , and energy and power densities of 0.625 Wh kg −1 and 150 W kg −1 , respectively. Structural analysis indicates negligible deformation, while the mechanical soundness of the structure is shown by von Mises stress. Under the bending condition, the symmetric flexible supercapacitor exhibits deformation‐induced changes in ionic diffusion pathways, resulting in a specific capacitance of 11.25 F g −1 , an energy density of 0.5625 Wh kg −1 , and a power density of 150 W kg −1 at 1 A g −1 .
articles.summary_en: Wiley research uses coupled electrochemical–mechanical simulations to assess a Mo₂C MXene/natural-rubber flexible supercapacitor under bending. Bending slightly reduces specific capacitance and energy density by altering ionic diffusion pathways, while maintaining structural integrity.

articles.title_original: Optimization of conductivity for MXene polymer nanocomposites by the number and diameter of contacts among adjacent nanosheets
articles.title_en: Model identifies contact factors governing MXene nanocomposite conductivity
articles.excerpt_original: In this study, a model for the conductivity of MXene-based samples is developed by simultaneously considering the percolation threshold, inter-nanosheet interfacial contacts, contact geometry, and electron tunneling effects. The percolation onset volume fraction and the network portion are demonstrated by interphase dimensions as well as the diameter and thickness of the MXene nanosheets. Accordingly, the proposed model is constructed based on physically meaningful and measurable parameters, providing an efficient framework for estimating the conductivity of MXene system. Parametric analysis and experimental conductivity facts from representative systems are employed to validate the method. The highest conductivity as 5.1 S/m is gained when nearly all MXene nanosheets participate in the conductive network and the interphase thickness is 40 nm. Furthermore, when the number of contact points reaches 40 and the contact circle diameter is 50 nm, the conductivity increases significantly, approaching 6.2 S/m. Overall, larger interphase region, shorter tunneling distance, larger contact area, higher contact number, and a greater fraction of networked nanoparticles lead to improved conductivity.
articles.summary_en: A conductivity model for MXene polymer nanocomposites integrates percolation, interfacial contact geometry, and electron tunneling. It indicates that larger contact areas, more contact points, shorter tunneling distances, and broader interphase regions can substantially improve conductivity, with modeled values reaching 6.2 S/m.

articles.title_original: High-Quality, Low-Cost Quasi-Bulk Hexagonal Boron Nitride Crystals by LP-HVPE: Machine Learning-Assisted Process Optimization via XRD and Raman Characterization
articles.title_en: Machine Learning Optimizes Low-Cost Growth of High-Quality hBN Crystals
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Highly ordered, quasi-bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) films were grown on c-plane sapphire (α-Al2O3) substrates via low-pressure hydride vapor-phase epitaxy (LP-HVPE), using industrial-grade boron trichloride (BCl3) and ammonia (NH3) as low-cost boron and nitrogen sources, respectively. The effects of four key growth parameters (growth temperature, III/V source flow ratio, growth ambient, and growth pressure) on the crystalline quality of hBN films were systematically investigated via the single-variable method. A gradient boosting regression machine learning (ML) model was constructed based on 24 groups of experimental datasets to achieve high-precision prediction of hBN crystalline quality, with determination coefficients (R2) of 0.96 and 0.94 for the prediction of X-ray diffraction and Raman characteristic peak full width at half maximum, respectively. The optimized growth condition was determined as follows: a growth temperature of 1350 °C, a III/V ratio of 1:3, N2 ambient, and a growth pressure of 100 Pa, which is consistent with the global optimal parameters obtained by Bayesian optimization combined with the ML model. This work provides a low-cost, high-efficiency route for the controllable preparation of high-quality quasi-bulk hBN crystals via LP-HVPE with ML-assisted optimization.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a low-pressure hydride vapor-phase epitaxy process for producing highly ordered, quasi-bulk hexagonal boron nitride using industrial-grade precursors. Machine-learning and Bayesian optimization identified growth conditions that improved crystalline-quality prediction, supporting more efficient hBN manufacturing.

articles.title_original: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications
articles.title_en: Review Examines Molecular Dynamics of Graphene Ionic-Liquid Supercapacitors
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphene and graphene-derived electrodes combined with ionic liquid electrolytes provide atomically well-defined, high-surface-area interfaces and wide electrochemical windows, making them benchmark platforms for supercapacitor research. Understanding how molecular-scale structure at this interface controls macroscopic capacitance requires molecular dynamics simulation since neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. This review treats the electrode-charging methods available─fixed and constant-charge, constant potential, electronic-structure-aware variants, and applied fields─together with force-field choice, as a toolbox of complementary tools suited to different questions, not a hierarchy of accuracy. We use this framework to organize findings on interfacial structure, electrode curvature, defects, doping, and nanoconfinement, emphasizing how these factors affect both the electric double layer and quantum capacitance. We conclude that progress toward predictive simulation will depend less on selecting a single optimal method than on integrating electrolyte polarizability, realistic electrode electronic response, structural complexity, and transferable machine-learning potentials within experimentally validated frameworks.
articles.summary_en: The review evaluates molecular-dynamics methods for studying graphene and graphene-derived electrodes with ionic-liquid electrolytes. It highlights interfacial structure, electrode response, defects, doping and nanoconfinement as factors governing electric-double-layer and quantum capacitance, and calls for experimentally validated, machine-learning-enabled simulations.

articles.title_original: Rheological evaluation of graphene oxide effects on geopolymer fresh properties
articles.title_en: Graphene oxide improves geopolymer rheology and thixotropy
articles.excerpt_original: Given their substantial potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, geopolymers have recently attracted significant interest as a cement replacement. Recent research has focused on incorporating various nanomaterials to improve the properties of these binders—specifically their rheology and thixotropy, which are often suboptimal. The rheological behaviour of potassium-based geopolymers (KGP) is strongly affected by the physicochemical properties of K + ions and their role in governing early geopolymer network formation. In this study, Graphene Oxide (GO) was evaluated as a rheological and thixotropic modifier for KGP. To address gaps in the existing literature, a systematic rheological characterisation of GO-modified KGP systems is presented, encompassing flow parameters, thixotropy, and chemical evolution. KGP systems (K 2 O: Al 2 O 3 : SiO 2 = 1:1:3) were synthesised with varying water molar ratios (10, 11, 12, and 13). Systems incorporating 0.02%, 0.04%, 0.06%, and 0.08% GO (at a 13-water molar ratio) were then systematically analysed and compared. Using Herschel-Bulkley (H B) model analysis, it was identified that critical modifications in the geopolymer flow parameters, such as increased yield stress and reduced fluidity index, occurred upon the addition of GO. Subsequently, significant enhancements in the thixotropy of the KGP were also identified during setting. Overall, critical rheological parameters of the KGP paste modified with GO nanoparticles were quantitatively characterised and analysed.
articles.summary_en: Academic research evaluates graphene oxide as a rheological and thixotropic modifier for potassium-based geopolymers, a potential lower-emission cement alternative. Adding 0.02–0.08% graphene oxide increased yield stress, reduced fluidity, and enhanced thixotropy during setting.

articles.title_original: Experimental Design Signatures Emerge from Topic Modeling of Graphene Oxide Literature
articles.title_en: Topic Modeling Maps Graphene Oxide Research and Experimental Parameters
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The literature on graphene oxide (GO) comprises hundreds of thousands of publications spanning synthesis, characterization, and applications in diverse domains. Advancing GO materials requires a structured knowledge map derived from systematic mining of this extensive corpus. However, extracting meaningful insights from this vast, heterogeneous, sparse, and unstructured data remains a challenge. To address this challenge, Natural Language Processing techniques, including topic modeling, community discovery, and parameter extraction, are here employed to establish a framework. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) was applied to the full text of more than 120,000 articles, enabling the identification of eight macro-domains within the GO literature, and neural topic modeling was subsequently employed to characterize the granularity and heterogeneity of these domains. Parameter extraction was performed using Large Language Models (LLMs) on a subset of 8000 full-text articles, with a proto-ontology incorporated into the extraction prompt. Even with a broad prompt, an F1 score of 94% was achieved against manual validation. The extracted parameters were then clustered through community modeling and compared with the LDA-derived topics. At this intermediate resolution of the literature, we demonstrate the application of a recommendation system for relevant parameters according to the material family and application domain. The applicability of the framework at higher resolutions was further demonstrated through the construction of a data set of CO2 adsorption for graphene- and GO-based materials. This data set was subsequently employed in a downstream predictive case study using an Extremely Randomized Trees Regressor, with different training-test splitting strategies eva
articles.summary_en: Researchers analyzed more than 120,000 graphene oxide publications using topic modeling and extracted experimental parameters from 8,000 full-text articles with reported high validation accuracy. The resulting framework supports parameter recommendations and a predictive case study on CO2 adsorption in graphene- and graphene-oxide materials.

articles.title_original: MXene ‐ MWCNTs Hybrid Reinforced PA6 Nanocomposites for Electronic Packaging Applications
articles.title_en: MXene–MWCNT Hybrids Boost PA6 Conductivity for Electronic Packaging
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT MXene is considered a promising 2D material for advanced thermal management, flexible electronics, and conductive polymer nanocomposites due to its high electrical conductivity, layered morphology, and tunable surface chemistry. In the present work, various MXene‐based hybrid fillers were prepared by functionalizing Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene with multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) in different ratios, namely M4C1, M2C1, and M1C1. The complete structural and microstructural characterization was performed to confirm the successful formation of the hybrids and to study the effect of the filler composition on the electrical transport properties. The MXene–MWCNTs hybrids showed the formation of a 3D interconnecting network between the MXene sheets and the MWCNTs. The charge transport behavior of the hybrid powders was affected by the existence of multiple contact interfaces. Moreover, the optimized hybrid filler (M4C1) was incorporated into a polyamide‐6 (PA6) matrix to prepare PA6–M4C1 nanocomposites. Structural analysis revealed that the semi‐crystalline nature of PA6 was preserved after incorporation of the MXene–MWCNTs hybrid filler; however, the degree of crystallinity was slightly decreased. The PA6–M4C1 nanocomposite showed a considerable increase in electrical conductivity due to the formation of a 3D interconnecting conductive network, which was enabled by the MWCNTs bridging in the polymer matrix. PA6‐based nanocomposites are widely applied in fields such as prevention of electrostatic discharge in electronic packaging, but also show potential for enhanced multifunctional performance. The present study shows that the MXene–MWCNTs hybrid systems are promising materials for the development of electrically conductive polymer nanocomposites for advanced electronic
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene–MWCNT hybrid fillers that form a three-dimensional conductive network in PA6 nanocomposites. The optimized formulation substantially increased electrical conductivity while preserving the polymer’s semicrystalline structure, supporting potential electrostatic-discharge protection in electronic packaging.

articles.title_original: Interfacially Regulated MXene‐Based Nanocomposite Membranes for Highly Selective Ion Transport and Salinity Gradient Energy Harvesting
articles.title_en: MXene membranes deliver selective ion transport and salinity-gradient energy harvesting
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Achieving high ion selectivity, low membrane resistance, and long‐term stability remains a key challenge in developing two‐dimensional nanomaterial polymer composite membranes, where interfacial interactions critically influence membrane structure and ion transport. Here, we report interfacially regulated MXene‐based nanocomposite membranes in which humic acid (HA) mediates interactions between Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheets and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix. Structural characterization together with molecular dynamics simulations indicates that HA incorporation modifies MXene organization and interfacial interactions within the membrane, which are associated with enhanced ion‐transport properties. The optimized membrane achieved near‐ideal monovalent cation selectivity (∼99%), a low area‐specific membrane resistance of 0.06 Ω·m 2 , and an energy conversion efficiency of 45.6%. The same membrane was evaluated over multiple electrochemical testing cycles totaling approximately 300 h, including dedicated 48 h stability measurements under heavy‐metal‐ and organic‐foulant‐containing conditions. A model‐based assessment of a conceptual reverse electrodialysis (RED) stack predicts a 37% increase in power generation, accompanied by an increase in energy conversion efficiency from 30.0% to 41.1%, relative to the commercial‐membrane scenario. These findings demonstrate that regulating interfacial interactions provides an effective design strategy for developing MXene‐based ion‐selective membranes for salinity‐gradient energy harvesting and related electrochemical separation processes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed humic-acid-regulated MXene membranes with approximately 99% monovalent cation selectivity, low resistance, and 45.6% energy-conversion efficiency. Extended testing and modeling indicate potential for more durable, higher-output reverse electrodialysis systems.

articles.title_original: Numerical investigation of sulfamoylbenzoic acid-functionalized MXene interface modifier for high-efficiency perovskite solar cells
articles.title_en: MXene Interface Modifier Boosts Perovskite Solar-Cell Efficiency to 25.15%
articles.excerpt_original: In the pursuit of sustainable, high-efficiency energy solutions, perovskite (PVT) solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as promising candidates due to their tunable optoelectronic properties and low-cost fabrication. However, commercialization remains hindered by efficiency stagnation and interfacial instability, particularly at the buried electron transport layer (ETL)/PVT interface. To address this, a novel interfacial modification strategy is proposed using MXene functionalized with 4-sulfamoylbenzoic acid (MX-Sba) as an interlayer at the ETL/PVT junction in cesium-formamidinium (CsFAMAPbIBr 2 )-based PSCs. The carboxylic acid–terminated MX-Sba improves conductivity, energy level alignment, and defect passivation, facilitating efficient charge extraction and reduced non-radiative recombination. Numerical simulations revealed favorable band bending, charge carrier mobility, and interfacial transport characteristics. A detailed analysis underscores the impact of interfacial defect density and resistance variations on charge dynamics and device performance. The optimized device exhibits a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.15%, with a short-circuit current density ([Formula: see text]) of 24.35[Formula: see text]mA/cm 2 , open-circuit voltage ([Formula: see text]) of 1.262[Formula: see text]V, and fill factor (FF) of 81.81%. These findings establish MX-Sba as a multifunctional interface modifier and outline a scalable pathway for developing efficient, durable PSCs for clean energy applications.
articles.summary_en: Numerical simulations indicate that sulfamoylbenzoic acid-functionalized MXene can improve conductivity, energy-level alignment, defect passivation, and charge extraction at the buried ETL/perovskite interface. The optimized simulated device reached a 25.15% power-conversion efficiency, suggesting a potential route toward more stable, scalable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title_original: Halogen Engineered Chiral Amplification in Chiral Hybrid 2D Perovskites for Self‐Powered Circularly Polarized Light Detection
articles.title_en: Halogen Engineering Enhances Chiral Perovskite Photodetectors
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Chiral hybrid perovskites hold great promise for optoelectronic and spintronic applications due to their superior optoelectronic properties. However, the development of self‐powered circularly polarized light (CPL) detectors is often hindered by weak chiroptical anisotropy and inefficient zero‐bias operation. Herein, we report the synthesis of chiral ( R/S ‐3BrMBA) 2 PbBr x I 4‐x (0 ≤ x ≤ 4) hybrid perovskites, demonstrating that halogen engineering is an effective strategy for chiral amplification. Through this approach, the g CD value is enhanced by more than 5‐fold, attributed to intensified octahedral distortion and the concomitant modulation of spin–orbit coupling. Remarkably, we achieved a Zeeman splitting of 0.663 meV, a 2.4‐fold increase over the pristine sample, which represents the highest value reported to date for chiral 2D perovskites. Furthermore, the (R‐3BrMBA) 2 PbBr 2 I 2 device exhibits an open‐circuit voltage exceeding 5 V, breaking the traditional bandgap limit while enabling self‐powered operation with a g Iph of 0.24. This work confirms halogen engineering as a robust strategy for chirality amplification, paving the way for advanced self‐driven chiral photodetectors.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used halogen engineering in chiral 2D hybrid perovskites to increase circular dichroism and Zeeman splitting. A self-powered detector achieved an open-circuit voltage above 5 V and improved circularly polarized photodetection, supporting advanced chiral optoelectronics.

articles.title_original: EL-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL MORPHIC SELF-COOLING CHIP ARCHITECTURE (E-TMSC) A Post-Moor's Law Paradigm Integrating Topological Insulators, Phase-Change Materials, and Spin-Caloritronics for Reconfigurable, Zero-Resistance, Thermodynamically Self-Sustaining Com
articles.title_en: Proposed Self-Cooling Topological Chip Architecture Integrates Phase-Change Computing and Spin-Caloritronics
articles.excerpt_original: The El-Rakhawi Topological Morphic Self-Cooling Chip Architecture (E-TMSC) is a post-Moor's Law computing paradigm integrating four synergistic physical phenomena: topological insulators (Bi₂Se₃) providing zero-resistance edge state transport, phase-change materials (Ge₂Sb₂Te₅) enabling morphic reconfiguration between CPU/GPU/NPU/memory architectures in <1 nanosecond, spin-caloritronic energy harvesting converting waste heat to useful power via Spin Seebeck Effect and Inverse Spin Hall Effect in heavy metal layers (Pt/W), and 2D van der Waals buffer layers (h-BN, 1-3 atomic layers) isolating topological edge states from thermal and lattice-mismatch stresses induced by PCM switching. The architecture achieves 70-80% energy reduction versus state-of-the-art GPUs, self-cooling operation without active thermal management, >10¹² switching cycle endurance, and intrinsic hardware-level security against side-channel attacks through quantized conductance independent of processed data. The morphic reconfiguration controller solves constrained optimization in hardware using PCM crossbar arrays, enabling real-time adaptation to workload, thermal, and security constraints. Compatible with modified CMOS fabrication processes, E-TMSC represents a fundamental phase transition from static lithographic circuits to dynamically reconfigurable, thermodynamically self-sustaining computation. (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23441641)
articles.summary_en: The E-TMSC concept combines Bi₂Se₃ topological insulators, Ge₂Sb₂Te₅ phase-change materials, spin-caloritronic heat harvesting and h-BN buffer layers for reconfigurable computing hardware. Claims of self-cooling operation, 70–80% energy savings and high switching endurance are presented in the publication and lack independent validation.

articles.title_original: Engineering performance of graphene nanoplatelet-modified pumice-based lightweight mortar
articles.title_en: Graphene nanoplatelets improve pumice-based lightweight mortar
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Pumice-based lightweight mortars generally exhibit high porosity, which adversely affects their engineering performance. This study investigated the influence of graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) on the fresh, physical, mechanical, and microstructural properties of pumice-based lightweight mortars. GNPs were incorporated at dosages of 0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, and 0.10 wt.% of cement, and the mortars were evaluated through flow diameter (FD), water absorption (WA), compressive strength (CS), flexural strength (FS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and ImageJ-based microstructural analysis. Increasing the GNP dosage from 0 to 0.10 wt.% reduced the FD from 207 to 186 mm, corresponding to a 10.1% decrease. Among the investigated mixtures, the mixture containing 0.03 wt.% GNP exhibited the best overall performance. At this dosage, WA decreased from 12.82% to 12.23%, representing a 4.60% reduction relative to the control mixture. The 28 d CS increased from 27.84 to 31.23 MPa, while the FS increased from 4.28 to 4.81 MPa, corresponding to improvements of 12.18% and 12.38%, respectively. ImageJ analysis showed that the two-dimensional void area decreased from 10.21% in the control mixture to 7.47% in the mixture containing 0.03 wt.% GNP, corresponding to a 26.84% reduction. SEM observations also indicated a denser and more homogeneous cementitious matrix at this dosage. Higher GNP dosages were associated with slight performance reductions and localized agglomeration of nanoplatelets. Overall, 0.03 wt.% GNP was the best-performing dosage among those investigated, improving the engineering performance and microstructural compactness of pumice-based lightweight mortars.
articles.summary_en: IOP Publishing research found that 0.03 wt.% graphene nanoplatelets delivered the best performance in pumice-based lightweight mortar, increasing 28-day compressive strength by 12.18% and flexural strength by 12.38%. The dosage also reduced water absorption and void area, while higher concentrations caused localized agglomeration and slight performance declines.

articles.title_original: Tailoring surface termination and intrinsic metal phase of MXene via Lewis acidic molten salt etching for electrocatalysis
articles.title_en: Lewis-acidic molten-salt etching enables tunable MXene electrocatalysts
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional transition metal carbides/nitrides/carbonitrides (MXene) have been widely applied in various electrocatalytic fields due to the unique layered structure, excellent intrinsic conductivity, tunable surface chemistry and high specific surface area. However, the traditional synthesis strategies of MXene involve dangerous fluorine-containing etching reagents, which have drawbacks such as strong corrosiveness, high safety risks and deficient active sites, thus severely limiting the regulation of active sites and the optimization of electrocatalytic performance. The Lewis acidic molten salt (LAMS) strategy utilizes the redox reaction between metal cations in the LAMS and the A-site atoms in the MAX phase to achieve selective etching and obtain MXene, featuring high safety, universality and structural controllability. More importantly, the LAMS strategy can simultaneously achieve surface termination modification and in-situ metal phase derivation during the etching process, ingeniously constructing dual functional site for electrocatalysis. This review comprehensively summarizes the structure and properties of MXene and the improvement methods and etching principles of the LAMS strategy. Additionally, the catalytic mechanism of surface termination and metal phase, and the latest progress in electrocatalysis are systematically sorted out. Furthermore, the currently challenges and the future prospects for the LAMS strategy are proposed. This review aims to break the conventional mindset of harmless treatment of etching by-products, as well as strengthen the resource utilization of LAMS derived by-products as active sites in electrocatalysis, providing new idea and theoretical reference for the development of green, low-cost and high-performance MXene-based catalys
articles.summary_en: A review examines Lewis acidic molten salt etching as a safer alternative to fluorine-based MXene synthesis. The approach enables controlled surface termination and in-situ metal-phase formation, potentially improving active-site design and electrocatalytic performance.

articles.title_original: Non-monotonic thickness dependence of MoS2–Sb contact resistance driven by bandgap and interlayer transport
articles.title_en: MoS₂–Sb Contact Resistance Varies Non-Monotonically with Thickness
articles.excerpt_original: Contact resistance at metal-two-dimensional semiconductor interfaces is a major factor limiting the performance of emerging two-dimensional electronic devices. Understanding how material thickness influences contact behavior is therefore essential for device optimization. Here, we systematically investigate the layer-dependent contact resistance of MoS2-Sb interfaces using MoS2 field-effect transistors with different layer numbers. Contact resistance was extracted using the transmission line method and compared for devices fabricated on SiO2 and HfO2 gate dielectrics. The results reveal a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of contact resistance on the MoS2 layer number. As the layer number increases from one to three, the contact resistance decreases and reaches a minimum value of 308 Ω·μm for trilayer MoS2, while further increasing the thickness leads to a rise in resistance. Analysis of the electronic band structure and interlayer transport mechanisms indicates that this behavior originates from the competition between bandgap reduction and increasing interlayer transport resistance. In the few-layer regime, bandgap narrowing lowers the Schottky barrier and reduces contact resistance, whereas in thicker layers the growing interlayer resistance dominates carrier transport. These findings provide important insight into thickness-dependent contact physics in two-dimensional semiconductors and offer practical guidance for optimizing contact engineering and channel thickness in next-generation electronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Academic research shows that contact resistance in MoS₂–Sb interfaces falls to 308 Ω·μm at trilayer thickness before rising in thicker films. The behavior reflects competition between bandgap narrowing and increasing interlayer transport resistance, informing contact and channel optimization in two-dimensional semiconductor devices.

articles.title_original: A Review on MXene and MXene-Based Composites for Advanced Biosensing and Bioimaging: Progress, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
articles.title_en: Review Highlights MXene Composites for Biosensing and Bioimaging
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Recently, the growth of two-dimensional (2D) materials has opened innovative paths in nanobiotechnology, and MXenes have emerged as leading candidates owing to their superior physicochemical performance and functional adaptability. MXenes, a family of transition metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides, reveal excellent electrical conductivity, large surface area, tuneable surface chemistry, hydrophilicity, and exceptional biocompatibility. These unique features make them highly attractive for biosensing and bioimaging applications. This review systematically abridges the recent advancements in MXene and its composites for biosensor development, containing electrochemical, optical, wearable, and flexible biosensors for the revealing of biomolecules, pathogens, cancer biomarkers, and glucose. The role of surface functionalization, hybridization with polymers, metal nanoparticles, carbon-based nanomaterials, and biomolecules in enhancing sensitivity, selectivity, and stability is critically deliberated. Moreover, the application of MXene composites in bioimaging approaches such as fluorescence imaging, photoacoustic imaging, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and multimodal imaging is explored, emphasizing their photothermal conversion efficiency and contrast development competences. Various challenges associated with long-term stability, oxidation resistance, toxicity, and large-scale production were also addressed, along with future perspectives for clinical translation and next-generation smart biomedical platforms. Overall, MXene-based materials clamp significant potential to transform biosensing and bioimaging techniques via multifunctional and integrated diagnostic systems.
articles.summary_en: A review examines MXene-based composites for electrochemical, optical, wearable, and flexible biosensors, as well as fluorescence, photoacoustic, MRI, and multimodal bioimaging. It identifies surface functionalization and hybridization strategies while noting unresolved challenges in stability, toxicity, oxidation resistance, and scale-up.

articles.title_original: Hexagonal boron nitride unlocks the mobile amorphous phase in PEO/NaFSI electrolyte
articles.title_en: hBN Doubles Ionic Conductivity in Solid-State Sodium Electrolytes
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has been reported to improve the ionic conductivity of solid polymer electrolytes for sodium batteries. We previously reported a four–fold increase in ionic conductivity in a poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and sodium bis (fluorosulfonylimide) (NaFSI) upon adding hBN at a concentration below the filler critical percolation threshold. However, the mechanism underpinning this enhanced conductivity was not clear. In the present work, we use quasi–elastic neutron scattering (QENS) to investigate polymer segmental dynamics in binary PEO/NaFSI and ternary PEO/NaFSI/hBN electrolytes at a fixed salt concentration of (Na+:EO = 0.05). For the ternary system the hBN concentration is above percolation. We explore the effects of confinement and interfacial behavior on polymer structure and conductivity while observing a doubling in ionic conductivity in the presence of hBN. QENS reveals that hBN leads to a nearly two–fold increase in the fraction of mobile amorphous polymer phase albeit at a lower average relaxation time. To complement the traditional considerations of charge carriers and polymer crystallinity, this study shows the mobile amorphous polymer phase plays a critical role in governing ionic conductivity.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used quasi-elastic neutron scattering to show that hexagonal boron nitride increases the mobile amorphous polymer phase in PEO/NaFSI electrolytes. The finding helps explain the observed near-doubling of ionic conductivity and could inform solid-state sodium-battery electrolyte design.

articles.title_original: Polarity‐Reconfigurable In 1.5 Mn 0.5 Se 3 Photodetectors Enabled by Asymmetric Schottky Barriers Toward Optical‐Electrical Logic Gates and Encryption Communication Application
articles.title_en: Mn-Doped In₂Se₃ Photodetectors Enable Polarity-Reconfigurable Optical Logic and Encryption
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Ensuring information security at the device level is a critical demand in the era of ubiquitous sensing and communication. In this work, we design an asymmetric two‐terminal Schottky photodetector based on Mn‐doped In 2 Se 3 . The regulation mechanism of Mn doping on electronic structure, interfacial charge distribution, and carrier transport is systematically investigated, and high‐performance optoelectronic logic operations and optical information encryption, decryption are realized. First‐principles calculations reveal that Mn doping can effectively narrow the bandgap of In 2 Se 3 from 1.0878 to 0.8986 eV and introduce donor impurity levels, significantly improving carrier concentration and optical absorption. Benefiting from the polarity‐tunable photoresponse enabled by asymmetric Schottky barriers, the device successfully implements multifunctional optoelectronic logic gates including XNOR, NAND, NOR etc. Furthermore, a complete optical information encryption and decryption system is constructed based on the XNOR logic, realizing secure encoding and accurate recovery of plaintext information. This work not only provides an effective strategy for doping modification and interface engineering of two‐dimensional semiconductors, but also offers new concepts and experimental support for high‐performance devices toward next‐generation optoelectronic computing and optical communication security.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed asymmetric Schottky photodetectors based on Mn-doped In₂Se₃, using bandgap engineering and tunable photoresponse to implement XNOR, NAND, and NOR logic gates. The devices also demonstrated optical information encryption and decryption, indicating potential relevance to secure optoelectronic computing and communications.

articles.title_original: Tunable quasi-BIC-enhanced graphene metasurface absorber
articles.title_en: Graphene metasurface achieves tunable 99.9% light absorption
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphene has garnered extensive attention due to its unique optoelectronic properties. However, its relatively weak light-matter interaction results in low absorption, limiting its applications in optoelectronic devices. The emergence of bound states in the continuum (BICs) offers a novel approach to enhancing light-matter interactions. However, most current research focuses on enhancing light absorption of graphene by exciting symmetry-protected quasi-BICs, which usually rely on asymmetric metasurface designs and thus increase fabrication complexity. In this paper, we design a graphene-based accidental quasi-BIC metasurface absorber. By exciting accidental quasi-BICs, we significantly enhance the absorption of monolayer graphene. We achieve an absorption as high as 99.9% using the proposed structure. We can also actively tune the quasi-BIC by modifying the graphene Fermi energy and geometric parameters. This work may offer novel insights into enhancing light absorption in graphene and other two-dimensional materials, and provide a reference for designing optoelectronic devices such as modulators, photodetectors, and optical sensors.
articles.summary_en: Researchers designed an accidental quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum graphene metasurface absorber that reportedly achieves up to 99.9% absorption in monolayer graphene. Tuning the graphene Fermi energy and geometry could support modulators, photodetectors, and optical sensors without requiring asymmetric metasurface designs.

articles.title_original: Dynamic surface chemistry of MXenes: Toward adaptive interfaces
articles.title_en: MXene Surface Chemistry Evolves Under Operating Conditions
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes are a class of two-dimensional materials whose tunable surface chemistry renders them promising for a wide range of applications, including catalysis and energy storage. Their surface chemistry is initially established during synthesis from their parent MAX phases through selective etching and serves as a key tunable parameter that governs MXenes’ functional properties and behavior. However, MXene surfaces are not static. Beyond synthesis, their surface terminations can be deliberately engineered, and, importantly, continue to evolve dynamically under chemical, electrochemical, and thermal operating conditions. Such transformations include termination removal, substitution, reconstruction, and protonation. Consequently, MXenes’ performance is governed by the in operando evolution of surface chemistry, rather than solely by the initial terminations introduced during synthesis or post-synthesis modifications. Embracing this dynamic paradigm reframes MXene surface chemistry from a synthetic descriptor to a design variable, opening opportunities to engineer reaction pathways, stabilize transient active states, and couple structure with function in real time. By conceptualizing MXene surfaces as dynamic interfaces, this article highlights how surface chemistry transforms under working conditions and how this evolution can be rationally harnessed to optimize performance in various applications, including catalysis and energy storage. MXene surface chemistry evolves from synthesis and post-synthesis processing to in operando conditions, where interactions with the working environment can further transform surface terminations andactive sites. Understanding and controlling this dynamic surface evolution provides a pathway to tailor MXene propertiesand optimize performanc
articles.summary_en: Research shows that MXene surface terminations continue to change during chemical, electrochemical, and thermal operation, rather than remaining fixed after synthesis. Controlling these dynamic interfaces could improve performance in energy-storage applications and catalysis.

articles.title_original: Boron nitride nanosheets filtration membrane for efficient separation of pollutant molecules from aqueous solution
articles.title_en: Boron Nitride Nanosheet Membrane Removes Water Pollutants
articles.excerpt_original: Two dimensional nanomaterials have exhibit promising performance in membrane science, especially hexagonal boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs) with inherent chemical inertness. Here, BNNSs membranes with compact and well-organized stacking texture were successfully prepared via vacuum-assisted filtration approach using chemo-mechanical exfoliated and functionalized BNNSs as matrix. The BNNSs with an average lateral dimension of ~100 nm have few layers structure and abundant hydroxyl and amino groups. The viscosity of the solvent and thickness of membrane are important factors affecting the permeability performance. Importantly, the BNNSs membranes exhibit fascinating filtration and separation performance for various pollutants in water, including abusive organic dyes, heavy metal ion and drugs. Specifically, the membrane with a typical thickness of 30 μm shows the water flux up to 2.1 L⋅m −2 ⋅min −1 ⋅bar −1 and 99.87% removal rate for tetracycline. These performances are not only caused by simple physical interception of BNNSs constructed nanochannels, but also by certain intermolecular chemical interactions between functional groups on BNNSs and pollutant molecules. This work would provide experimental foundation and analytical experience for the practical application of BNNSs membranes in the field of complex water purification.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a functionalized hexagonal boron nitride nanosheet membrane using vacuum-assisted filtration. A 30 μm membrane achieved water flux of up to 2.1 L·m⁻²·min⁻¹·bar⁻¹ and 99.87% tetracycline removal, alongside separation of dyes and heavy-metal ions.

articles.title_original: Flexible 2D Perovskite–hBN Optoelectronic Dendritic Neurons for Energy-Efficient Information Processing
articles.title_en: Flexible hBN–Perovskite Dendritic Neurons Enable Low-Power Neuromorphic Processing
articles.excerpt_original: Artificial dendrites, capable of nonlinear signal integration, are key building blocks for next-generation neuromorphic hardware, yet their realization in soft, solution-processed materials remains hindered by instability and poorly controlled ion dynamics. Here, we report an artificial dendrite element based on a vertically orchestrated ITO/Ag nanoparticle (NP)/hBN/(PEA)2MA4Pb5I16/Pt NPS/ITO heterostructure, where a monolayer hBN barrier governs metal-ion injection with atomic precision. The hBN-mediated field redistribution enables graded and time-dependent filament initiation within the oriented two-dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite, producing highly nonlinear current integration analogous to excitatory postsynaptic potentials. Under consecutively correlated stimuli, the device exhibits hallmark dendritic behaviors-temporal summation, threshold-dependent firing, refractory period, and wavelength-sensitive integration-arising from controlled Ag+ accumulation and reversible filament branching. The devices operate at ∼1 V, demonstrate stable and reproducible transient responses over >1011 cycles, and retain robust performance under mechanical deformation. Complementary physics-based numerical modeling and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the influence of hBN on Ag+ diffusivity, as well as on filament formation. The dendritic neurons can efficiently encode velocity and direction, enabling compact feature maps for accurate motion classification and trajectory tracking. Our results introduce a promising material platform for high-density, energy-efficient neuromorphic processors capable of bio-inspired spatiotemporal learning.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a flexible artificial dendrite using an hBN barrier and 2D perovskite that controls Ag+ filament formation for nonlinear signal integration. The device operates at about 1 V, withstands more than 10^11 cycles, and supports motion classification and trajectory tracking, indicating potential for compact neuromorphic hardware.

articles.title_original: Stacking‐Tuned Phonon Renormalization and Effective Heat Transport in Moiré Semiconductor Superlattices
articles.title_en: Moiré semiconductor stacking controls phonon renormalization and heat transport
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Optically driven moiré semiconductor bilayers involve coupled phonon anharmonicity, interlayer interactions, and local heat dissipation, but experimental benchmarks across supported homo‐ and heterobilayers remain limited. Here, we combine temperature‐dependent Raman spectroscopy, excitation‐power‐dependent Raman thermometry, and photoluminescence to study twisted MoS 2 /MoS 2 , WS 2 /WS 2 , and MoS 2 /WS 2 bilayers. From 90 to 300 K, both homobilayers show conventional softening of Raman‐active phonons with negative effective anharmonic coefficients. In contrast, the WS 2 ‐derived out‐of‐plane A ‐mode in the MoS 2 /WS 2 heterobilayer hardens with increasing temperature, exhibiting a positive linear temperature coefficient of +0.00700 ± 0.00029 cm − 1 K − 1 and a positive effective Balkanski coefficient of +1.28 ± 0.19 cm − 1 , while other modes remain softening‐dominant. Photoluminescence reveals an interlayer excitonic channel only in the heterobilayer, indicating an interface‐specific phonon renormalization pathway beyond equilibrium anharmonic decay. Using two excitation objectives with distinct laser‐heating radii, the supported Raman thermometry resolves mode‐dependent effective thermal‐transport parameters and reduces covariance in extracting in‐plane heat‐transport and heat‐sinking coefficients. We further develop a physics‐guided monolayer‐to‐stacked neural‐network framework to reconstruct Raman spectra across temperature and power conditions and identify optimal optothermal regimes. These results establish heterointerface‐controlled phonon renormalization as a key factor in phonon dynamics controlling heat dissipation and provide a scalable platform for thermal design in moiré quantum devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used Raman spectroscopy, thermometry and photoluminescence to show that stacking and heterointerfaces in MoS₂/WS₂ bilayers alter phonon temperature responses and effective heat-transport parameters. The findings support thermal design of moiré quantum and semiconductor devices using physics-guided spectral modeling.

articles.title_original: MXene Film/Foam Bilayer Anodes with Enhanced Electrochemical Performance for Self-Standing Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.title_en: MXene Film/Foam Bilayer Improves Self-Standing Lithium-Ion Battery Anodes
articles.excerpt_original: The structural design of self-standing electrodes without binders and current collectors is critical for maximizing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, yet achieving electrical conductivity, ion accessibility, and mechanical integrity in a single architecture remains challenging. Although Ti3C2Tx MXene is a promising candidate, owing to its high metallic conductivity and structural robustness, conventional dense films suffer from restacking-induced restricted electrolyte penetration and Li+ diffusion. Conversely, porous MXene foams can mitigate restacking but exhibit weak electrical contact and limited mechanical robustness. To overcome this structural trade-off, we designed a self-standing MXene film/foam bilayer anode integrating a compact film layer with a porous foam layer, which was followed by air annealing to generate TiO2/TiOx-containing active sites. Among the various film/foam ratios systematically evaluated, the optimal 2:8 bilayer electrode exhibited low charge-transfer resistance and fast redox kinetics, delivering 83.24 mAh g−1 at 1000 mA g−1 and retaining 195.12 mAh g−1 at 50 mA g−1 after 200 cycles, outperforming the single-architecture electrodes. These results demonstrate that the bilayer design effectively combines the structural and electrical stability of the film with the rapid ion transport and abundant active sites of the foam, offering a promising strategy for high-performance self-standing anodes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a Ti3C2Tx MXene film/foam bilayer anode that combines compact-film conductivity and mechanical stability with foam-enabled ion transport. The optimized 2:8 structure delivered 195.12 mAh g−1 at 50 mA g−1 after 200 cycles, outperforming single-architecture electrodes.

However, achieving controlled graphene characteristics, retaining its functionality during manufacturing, and developing scalable incorporation methods remain important challenges. This thesis investigates these aspects through graphene oxide (GO) deposition on metallic powders, the retention and tribological performance of graphene-based materials in thermal spraying, and the influence of GO on the laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) processing of pure copper.A molecular-level mixing method was developed to deposit GO onto metallic powder particles using APTES as a coupling agent. Adjusting the APTES concentration and GO loading enabled control over coating characteristics and surface coverage. By adapting the mixing conditions and chemical parameters, the methodology was scaled from 20 to 500 g batches that were repeatedly used to produce 10 kg of GO-coated copper powder.Graphene retention and tribological functionality were investigated in Al₂O₃ coatings containing graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs), produced by suspension plasma spraying, and GO-containing WC–Co–Cr coatings, produced by high-velocity air-fuel spraying. Graphene-based materials were retained after deposition in both systems but underwent progressive structural and chemical modification during sliding wear. Synchrotron X-ray spectromicroscopy revealed GNPs retention at the alumina tribosurface, accompanied by carbon redistribution and amorphization beneath the wear track. This review summarizes research on the fabrication of 3D structures using nanosheet-based inks and composite feedstocks—including graphene and its derivatives, MXenes, transition metal dichalcogenides, hexagonal boron nitride, and black phosphorus. Applications in sensing, energy storage devices, and biomedical scaffolds demonstrate the immense potential of these methods, while printed optoelectronic devices are discussed as a complementary case of device integration. articles.title_original: Casimir forces on suspended thin dielectric membranes covered with graphene
articles.title_en: Graphene-Coated Membranes Enhance Thermal Casimir Effects
articles.excerpt_original: We investigate the Casimir force on thin suspended dielectric layers covered with graphene, both theoretically and experimentally. Thermal effects of the Casimir force on graphene occur at separations significantly smaller compared to ordinary metals and dielectrics. At such small separations, the Casimir force is sufficiently strong to be measured experimentally. However, the presence of substrates to support the graphene significantly reduces the enhancement. We show theoretically that replacing the solid substrate beneath graphene with a thin dielectric membrane partially restores this strong thermal dependence. One of the interacting objects is a solid gold plate. The other object is a suspended dielectric membrane made of either 15 nm of silicon oxide or 13 nm silicon nitride, covered with graphene. At a separation of $\sim$500 nm, theoretical predictions yield changes in the Casimir pressure of up to 54 % and 40 % for silicon oxide and silicon nitride, respectively, when the temperature is increased from 10 K to 294 K. Measurements were performed for graphene on a suspended silicon nitride membrane at room temperature, using a gold-coated sphere attached to a cantilever as the force sensor. The measured force gradient is consistent with the theoretical prediction, although the thermal dependence could not be resolved, in part because of uncertainties in the optical properties of silicon nitride. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin dielectric membrane covered with graphene provides a substantial reduction of the Casimir force, which may facilitate the stable operation of neutral nanomechanical elements at small separations.
articles.summary_en: Researchers theoretically and experimentally studied Casimir forces between gold and suspended dielectric membranes coated with graphene. Replacing a bulk substrate with a thin membrane substantially strengthens thermal dependence and could support stable neutral nanomechanical elements at submicron separations.

articles.title_original: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
articles.title_en: Graphene–PEDOT:PSS Solar Cells Reach 8.52% Efficiency with Improved Stability
articles.excerpt_original: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.
articles.summary_en: A planar PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-type silicon Schottky solar cell achieved 8.52% power conversion efficiency, compared with 4.56% for a graphene/silicon reference cell. Graphene also protected the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS layer, enabling approximately 90% efficiency retention after 75 days of ambient exposure.

articles.title_original: A review of dispersion mechanisms in graphene reinforced ABS nanocomposites for additive manufacturing
articles.title_en: Review examines graphene dispersion in ABS composites for 3D printing
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Due to the enhanced mechanical, thermal, electrical, and tribological performance graphene-reinforced Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) nanocomposites have emerged as promising materials for fused deposition modeling (FDM). However, realizing these improvements remains challenging because of graphene agglomeration and weak interfacial adhesion with the ABS matrix. This review significantly examines the impact of dispersion mechanisms and interfacial engineering on the performance of graphene–ABS nanocomposites. Different graphene derivatives, including graphene oxide (GO), reduced graphene oxide (rGO), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs), are compared with respect to their dispersion behavior, compatibility with ABS, and reinforcement efficiency. Processing techniques such as melt blending, solvent-assisted processing, and in-situ polymerization, together with functionalization strategies, are comprehensively reviewed. Reported studies indicate 25–45% improvement in tensile strength, 30–60% enhancement in fracture toughness, 20–50% increase in elastic modulus, 2–5 folds enhancement in thermal conductivity, 10–30 °C improvement in thermal stability, 30–70% reduction in wear rate and significant enhancement in electrical conductivity through percolation network formation with optimised graphene loading and processing. The review explores the relationships between structure, processing, and properties in grapheme–ABS nanocomposites. It highlights gaps in current research and offers practical design guidelines, along with future research directions, aimed at developing high-performance multifunctional materials for advanced additive manufacturing applications.
articles.summary_en: A review analyzes how dispersion mechanisms, interfacial engineering, and processing methods affect graphene-reinforced ABS nanocomposites for fused deposition modeling. It reports improved mechanical, thermal, wear, and electrical properties while identifying agglomeration and weak interfacial adhesion as persistent challenges.

articles.title_original: Ferrite and reduced graphene oxide-ferrite nanocomposites as nanohybrid materials
articles.title_en: Reduced Graphene Oxide–Ferrite Nanocomposites Show Promise for Drug Delivery and Supercapacitors
articles.excerpt_original: The successful eco-friendly synthesis of Ca 1-x Co x Fe 2 O 4 nanoferrites and magnetic nanocomposites of calcium-cobalt ferrite with reduced graphene oxide (rGO/Ca 1-x Co x Fe 2 O 4 ) has been reported via a thermal treatment method in the presence of rosemary leaf extract. The synthesized nanomaterials were characterized using various physicochemical techniques. Their possible application as both drug delivery nanocarriers and as electrode materials for supercapacitors has been described. For investigating how toxic nanocarriers (NCs) are when used in drug delivery platforms, the MTT assay served as the measurement tool. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) characterizations of the CaF nanoferrite and rGO/CF37 nanocomposite samples highlighted the excellent performances as supercapacitors, with specific capacitance (C S ) values, under the condition of 5 mV/s scan rate, giving 822 and 802F/g, respectively. This green preparation protocol of nanoferrites and magnetic nanocomposites of calcium-cobalt ferrite with reduced graphene oxide, by controlling biocompatibility and electrochemical properties, offers remarkable advantages, including environmental friendliness and good efficiency, suitable for biomedical field applications, like wastewater treatment and water desalination.
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized calcium–cobalt ferrite/reduced graphene oxide nanocomposites using rosemary leaf extract and evaluated their physicochemical, biological, and electrochemical properties. The materials demonstrated specific capacitances up to 802 F/g and potential applications in drug delivery, wastewater treatment, water desalination, and supercapacitors.

articles.title_original: Layer-polarized PN and point junctions in double bilayer graphene
articles.title_en: Researchers Demonstrate Layer-Polarized PN and Point Junctions in Double Bilayer Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: We fabricate twisted double bilayer graphene devices with zero twist angle and a set of local top and bottom gates aligned perpendicularly to each other. A 1D PN junction can be electrostatically defined when the gate voltages applied to the top gates are the same but different on the bottom gates. Resistance peaks are observed at finite doping instead of at the charge neutrality points, exhibiting an unconventional broken-cross shape that arises from layer polarization of the P and N region, which can be further enhanced with finite magnetic fields. A 0D point junction (PJ) can be electrostatically defined by applying different gate voltages to the top and bottom gates, such that the P and N sides of the device are connected at a single point in the center of the device. As finite magnetic field B increases, the quantum Hall (QH) states are selectively brought into contact or away from each other depending on their layer polarization, leading to unconventional quantum oscillations which characterize the layer-polarized band-crossing. Our work provides new insights into understanding band-structure evolution and layer polarization in twisted bilayers and paves the way for new device functionality based on manipulating layer-polarized electronic states.
articles.summary_en: Researchers fabricated gated twisted double bilayer graphene devices and demonstrated electrostatically defined one-dimensional PN and zero-dimensional point junctions. Magnetic-field-dependent quantum Hall behavior revealed tunable layer-polarized electronic states, highlighting potential functionality for graphene-based electronic devices.

articles.title_original: Polymer-engineered MXenes for electrochemical sensors and biosensing
articles.title_en: Polymer engineering advances MXene electrochemical sensors
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) MXenes have rapidly emerged as one of the most promising materials for electrochemical sensors and biosensors owing to their high electrical conductivity, hydrophilic surfaces, large specific surface area, and versatile surface chemistry. However, their practical implementation remains limited by rapid oxidation, interlayer restacking, chemical instability, biofouling, and insufficient long-term operational reliability. Polymer engineering has appeared more than just a simple stabilization strategy, by tailoring MXene interfaces, regulating charge transport, enhancing structural stability, improving biomolecule immobilization, suppressing nonspecific adsorption, and optimizing electrochemical sensing performance. This review establishes a polymer-engineering framework that correlates polymer design, interface engineering, physicochemical properties, sensing mechanisms, device performance, and practical implementation through structure–property–performance relationships. Polymer integration strategies, i.e ., physical blending, surface functionalization, in situ and ex situ polymerization, layer-by-layer (LBL) assembly, and electrospinning are critically compared together with the functional roles of conductive, biocompatible, antifouling, molecularly imprinted, redox-active, and stimuli-responsive polymers. The review further evaluates advantages, limitations, and application-specific trade-offs associated with these engineering strategies across biomedical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, food safety, wearable and implantable devices, point-of-care systems, and advanced integrated sensing platforms. Finally, the remaining challenges associated with long-term stability, reproducibility, standardization, scalable manufacturing, clinical validat
articles.summary_en: A review examines polymer-integration strategies that address MXene oxidation, restacking, biofouling, and instability in electrochemical sensors and biosensors. It links polymer design and interface engineering to performance across biomedical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, food safety, and wearable and implantable devices, while noting remaining challenges in reproducibility, standardization, scale-up, and validation.

articles.title_original: Multifunctional pDA@MXene-enriched silk fibroin/PLLA nanofibrous scaffold with local piezoresponse for neural tissue engineering
articles.title_en: MXene-Enhanced Nanofibrous Scaffold Shows Promise for Neural Tissue Engineering
articles.excerpt_original: Neural tissue engineering requires functional scaffolds that provide structural support while presenting biomimetic physicochemical cues to cells. Incorporating stimulus-responsive functionality into electrospun scaffolds has emerged as a promising strategy for developing next-generation neural tissue engineering platforms. In this study, a polydopamine (pDA)@MXene-enriched silk fibroin/poly(L-lactic acid) (SF/PLLA) electrospun nanofibrous scaffold was developed as a multifunctional platform for neural tissue engineering. Structural and physicochemical characterization verified the formation of Ti3C2 MXene from the Ti3AlC2 MAX precursor, successful pDA functionalization, and effective vacuum-assisted incorporation of pDA@ Ti3C2 MXenes onto the SF/PLLA nanofibrous scaffold. PFM analysis revealed a detectable local electromechanical response, consistent with the piezo-responsive characteristics of the developed scaffold. Moreover, pDA@MXene incorporation enhanced the surface hydrophilicity, as evidenced by the decrease in water contact angle from 73.49 ± 0.73° to 47.38 ± 0.6°. In-vitro experiments showed that the developed scaffold supported PC-12 cell metabolic activity throughout the culture period. SEM observations revealed effective attachment and close cell-nanofiber interactions. Under NGF-treated conditions, following a commonly used 7-day PC12 differentiation period, βIII-tubulin-positive cells with neuron-like morphological features were observed on the pDA@MXene-enriched scaffold, supporting its compatibility with NGF-induced neuronal-like phenotypic development. Collectively, the pDA@MXene-enriched scaffold exhibited enhanced surface hydrophilicity, favorable mechanical properties, local electromechanical responsiveness, and cytocompatibility, supporting its po
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a polydopamine-functionalized Ti₃C₂ MXene/silk fibroin–PLLA nanofibrous scaffold with local piezoresponse, improved hydrophilicity, and favorable mechanical properties. In vitro testing indicated cytocompatibility and support for neuron-like PC-12 cell development, positioning the material as a candidate for neural tissue engineering.

articles.title_original: From Atoms to Cells: First‐Principles Mapping of MXene–TMD Heterostructures for Next‐Generation Metal‐Ion Batteries
articles.title_en: First-Principles Framework Maps MXene–TMD Battery Heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT MXene–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures combine tunable surface terminations with redox‐active layered hosts, offering a versatile platform for next‐generation metal‐ion batteries. This review introduces an evidence‐graded, atoms‐to‐cells framework that maps interface‐controlled descriptors—termination chemistry, interlayer spacing, charge redistribution, and mechanical compliance—from atomic‐scale computation to cell‐level performance across lithium, sodium, potassium, zinc, magnesium, calcium, and aluminum chemistries. Density functional theory (DFT) evidence is compiled separately from experimental evidence to enforce falsifiability: each design‐rule claim is graded as convergent, computation‐led, experiment‐led, or open. Computation reveals that MXene termination identity (–O/–OH/–F) shifts work functions by up to ∼3.5 eV and dominates adsorption energetics, diffusion barriers, and interfacial stability, while TMD phase (2H vs. 1T/1T′) controls conductivity and ion accessibility. Experimentally, MXene–TMD architectures consistently improve rate capability and cycling stability through restacking suppression and electronic percolation, yet most demonstrations remain at low areal loading, and interface persistence under realistic conditions is rarely verified. Critical gaps—including MXene oxidation drift, cost‐performance parity with carbon scaffolds, and insufficient operando validation—are identified alongside a decisive roadmap prioritizing termination‐aware design, thick‐electrode benchmarking, and closed‐loop descriptor‐to‐observable validation chains for practical deployment.
articles.summary_en: A review maps how MXene surface terminations and TMD phases influence adsorption, ion diffusion, conductivity, and interface stability across multiple metal-ion battery chemistries. It highlights improved rate capability and cycling stability but identifies low areal loading, oxidation, cost, and limited operando validation as barriers to deployment.

articles.title_original: Gradient Pore Engineering of MXene-Based Foam Evaporators for Efficient Solar Interfacial Evaporation and Evaporation-Induced Electricity Generation
articles.title_en: Gradient-Engineered MXene Foam Enables Solar Freshwater Production and Power Generation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Solar-driven interfacial evaporation coupled with evaporation-induced electricity generation offers a promising route for simultaneous freshwater production and low-grade energy harvesting, but its performance is often limited by the trade-off among water transport, heat localization, and ion migration. Here, an MXene-based porous foam evaporator with coupled pore-size and wettability gradients was fabricated through prefreezing and freeze-drying. The resulting architecture comprised a small-pore upper layer, an interconnected middle layer, and a large-pore bottom layer, enabling localized heating, continuous capillary water supply, rapid vapor escape, and directional ion transport. Benefiting from the broadband photothermal response of MXene and the hydrophilic PAAm-SA network, the optimized evaporator achieved solar absorptance above 90% and an evaporation rate of 1.44 kg m–2 h–1 under one sun, and an equivalent evaporation enthalpy of approximately 1.43 kJ g–1. After 100 h, 94.4% of the initial evaporation rate was retained. The device also exhibited stable electrical output, with voltage and current retentions of 93.4% and 90.1%, respectively. This work provides a simple strategy for integrating solar-driven interfacial evaporation and evaporation-induced electricity generation.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a porous MXene foam evaporator with graded pore sizes and wettability to improve water transport, heat localization, vapor escape, and ion migration. Under one sun, it achieved a 1.44 kg m⁻² h⁻¹ evaporation rate while retaining 94.4% performance after 100 hours and generating stable evaporation-induced electricity.
