It highlights mechanical reinforcement, bioactivity, matrix production, and cell–graphene interaction mechanisms, while outlining translational opportunities.

articles.title_original: Polymer-modified MXene thin-film nanocomposite membranes for forward osmosis
articles.title_en: Polymer-Modified MXene Membranes Improve Forward-Osmosis Performance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. The approach involves synthesizing MXene-functionalized polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-g-MXene) additives through a facile chemical grafting method, where hydroxyl groups serve as linkers to covalently bond PVP onto the surface of 2D MXene nanosheets. Subsequently, PVP-g-MXene is incorporated into a polyamide (PA) thin film via interfacial polymerization (IP) to produce the innovative TFN-FO membranes. Characterization of MXene and PVP-g-MXene was performed using FT-IR, XRD, TGA, and FE-SEM. The fabricated membranes were analyzed for surface morphology, roughness, and hydrophilicity using FESEM, AFM, and water contact angle (WCA) measurements. The results indicate that incorporating PVP-g-MXene significantly alters the physicochemical properties of the membranes, including morphology, roughness, hydrophilicity, and overall performance during the IP process. All modified membranes demonstrated improved water flux compared to the pristine TFC membrane, with TFN-PgM1 and TFN-PgM2 exhibiting superior selectivity. Notably the representative TFN-PgM2 membrane exhibited a water flux of 18.5 LMH, which is approximately 72% higher than that of the TFC membrane, and demonstrated a Js/Jw ratio of 0.167, indicating an 18.1% improvement in selectivity performance. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of polymer-modified MXene for the development of high-performance FO membranes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed polyvinylpyrrolidone-grafted MXene thin-film nanocomposite membranes for forward osmosis. The best membrane increased water flux by approximately 72% and improved selectivity by 18.1% versus a pristine thin-film composite membrane.

articles.title_original: Fabrication and Characterization of Wet-Spun Ti3C2Tx MXene Fibers
articles.title_en: Wet-Spun MXene Fibers Reach 446 S/cm Conductivity
articles.excerpt_original: MXene fibers have attracted considerable attention for flexible electronics and wearable devices owing to their high electrical conductivity and solution processability. The morphology and electrical conductivity of wet-spun MXene fibers are strongly influenced by fabrication conditions. Continuous Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene fibers were fabricated by wet spinning using colloidal dispersions with concentrations ranging from 25 to 80 mg mL-1. Fiber morphology and electrical conductivity were evaluated as a function of dispersion concentration. The electrical conductivity showed an increasing trend with concentration, reaching 446.06 S cm-1 for fibers prepared from the 80 mg mL-1 dispersion, compared with 58.95 S cm-1 for fibers prepared from the 25 mg mL-1 dispersion. This improvement is attributed to enhanced interflake contact and improved connectivity between MXene nanosheets at higher concentrations. Overall, the results demonstrate the successful fabrication of continuous MXene fibers across a range of dispersion concentrations and clarify the relationship between processing conditions, fiber morphology, and electrical conductivity, providing guidance for the optimization of MXene fiber fabrication for flexible electronic applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers fabricated continuous Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene fibers by wet spinning and examined how dispersion concentration affects morphology and conductivity. Conductivity increased from 58.95 to 446.06 S/cm as concentration rose from 25 to 80 mg/mL, supporting optimization for flexible electronics and wearable devices.

articles.title_original: Interfacial engineering of NiO-carbon black decorated MXene for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors
articles.title_en: NiO–MXene/carbon black composite improves asymmetric supercapacitor performance
articles.excerpt_original: MXene is a conductive and mechanically robust two-dimensional material that suffers from fewer redox-active charge storage sites and self-aggregation. MXene was synthesized from the MAX phase by LiF/HCl etching. Carbon black (CB) nanoparticles were then intercalated between the MXene sheets to suppress restacking and to form conductive pathways, after which NiO was introduced to supply additional redox-active sites while the conductive MXene/CB backbone maintained efficient electron transport. Formation of the composite and its counterparts was verified by physicochemical characterization. In a three-electrode configuration, the tri-material composite exhibits higher current density, longer galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) time, and a high areal capacitance (140.18 mF cm −2 ), which is 1.6 times that of MXene/CB (86.72 mF cm −2 ) and 3.4 times that of pristine MXene (40.8 mF cm −2 ). The fabricated ASC device (NiO@MXene/CB//CB) exhibits an areal capacitance of 46.8 mF cm −2 , an energy density of 6.50 μWh cm −2 at a power density of 1.50 mW cm −2 , a device-level rate capability of 69.2%, and a capacitance retention of about 74.5% after 8000 cycles. DFT calculations indicate a NiO-mediated interfacial charge redistribution, consistent with the improved electrochemical performance observed experimentally. This work provides an economically viable route to mitigate two intrinsic limitations of MXene electrodes.
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered a NiO–MXene/carbon black composite to reduce MXene restacking and add redox-active sites. The material achieved 140.18 mF cm−2 areal capacitance and retained about 74.5% capacity after 8,000 cycles in an asymmetric supercapacitor device.

articles.title_original: MXene‐Based Electrocatalysts for Sustainable Nitrogen Conversion: From Ammonia Oxidation to Nitrogen and Nitrate Reduction
articles.title_en: Review Highlights MXene Electrocatalysts for Sustainable Nitrogen Conversion
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT 2D transition‐metal carbides and nitrides, known as MXenes, have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for nitrogen‐related reactions, including ammonia oxidation (AOR), nitrogen reduction (NRR), and nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR). Their appeal stems from a layered architecture, abundant active sites, tunable surface chemistry, and high electrical conductivity. Key physicochemical properties—including controllable surface terminations (–O, –OH, –F), defect‐rich surfaces, and flexible electronic structures—facilitate intermediate adsorption and activation while enhancing charge‐transfer kinetics. Recent synthesis methods, such as HF etching and fluorine‐free Lewis acid approaches, enable precise control over functionalities that dictate catalytic performance. Furthermore, engineering strategies like heteroatom doping, defect engineering, and hybrid composite formation are explored to optimize activity, selectivity, and durability. Ti 3 C 2 T X remains the most extensively studied platform due to its versatility and performance. This review provides a comprehensive overview of advancements in MXene‐based catalysts for NO 3 RR, NRR, and AOR, highlighting the relationships between reaction mechanisms, electronic structures, and synthesis strategies. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for the rational design of efficient, scalable, and sustainable MXene catalysts for nitrogen‐related energy applications are discussed.
articles.summary_en: This review examines MXene-based catalysts for ammonia oxidation, nitrogen reduction, and nitrate reduction, emphasizing surface chemistry, defects, conductivity, and synthesis methods. It identifies Ti₃C₂Tₓ as the leading platform while outlining challenges in catalyst scalability, sustainability, activity, selectivity, and durability.

articles.title_original: CdS Nanocrystals Grown on MXene Frameworks for Stable Lithium−Sulfur Batteries
articles.title_en: CdS–MXene Frameworks Improve Lithium–Sulfur Battery Stability
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Lithium−sulfur (Li−S) batteries have been widely studied in recent years due to their high theoretical specific capacity and high energy density. However, the S cathode is plagued by issues of low electrical conductivity, shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs), and slow transformation kinetics, resulting in low rate performance and rapid capacity fading of Li−S batteries. Here, CdS nanocrystals with ultrafine size are grown in situ on accordion-like and highly conductive Ti3C2 MXene frameworks by a simple and low-temperature (60 °C) hydrothermal reaction. The loading of CdS nanocrystals on MXene is controlled by regulating the amount of precursors. The functional groups on MXene can act as nucleation sites to promote the uniform growth of CdS nanocrystals among the MXene frameworks. Besides, the accordion-like structure of MXene can restrict the excessive growth of CdS. The fabricated CdS/MXene composite with sufficient adsorption and catalytic active sites can effectively block the shuttle effect and accelerate the transformation of LiPSs, thus relieving the issues of the S cathode. Under the coordinated regulation of MXene frameworks and in situ-grown CdS nanocrystals, Li−S batteries exhibit superior cycling performance and rate capability.
articles.summary_en: Researchers grew ultrafine CdS nanocrystals in situ on conductive Ti3C2 MXene frameworks using a low-temperature hydrothermal process. The composite provides adsorption and catalytic sites that suppress lithium polysulfide shuttling and accelerate sulfur conversion, improving cycling performance and rate capability.

articles.title_original: Pore Morphology Modulates Piezoelectric Output in Fluorinated Polyimide-MXene Foam-Based Sensors for Intelligent Wearables
articles.title_en: Pore morphology improves MXene foam sensor performance for wearables
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Fluorinated polyimide (FPI) foam-based sensors with exceptional performance and unique piezoelectric properties have attracted extensive attention for applications in smart wearable electronics and the Internet of Things (IoT) systems. However, conventional foam-based sensors struggle to determine the extent to which the intrinsic triboelectricity caused by the porous structure affects the sensor’s overall electrical output performance. This work integrated the effect of pore morphology on the electrical performance of MXene-filled foam via the hot-pressing process to construct a foam sheet. This design alters the original pore structure of the foam, effectively mitigating the intrinsic triboelectric effect and providing a comparative analysis of the impact of the pore structure on the overall piezoelectric electrical output performance of the foam-based sensor. Furthermore, this integrated sensor enables combining IoT connectivity with medical monitoring applications, providing comprehensive user activity data through real-time monitoring and recognition. The research in this paper provides a research basis for the design and performance regulation of porous material-based sensors and holds profound implications for the advancement of wearable electronics and IoT sensing technology.
articles.summary_en: Researchers studied how pore structure affects the electrical output of fluorinated polyimide foams filled with MXene, using hot pressing to reduce intrinsic triboelectric effects. The resulting sensor supports real-time activity monitoring and IoT-enabled medical applications.

articles.title_original: PRECURSOR COMPOSITION AND TWO-STAGE THERMAL PROCESSING FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF NANOCRYSTALLINE HEXAGONAL BORON NITRIDE
articles.title_en: Two-Stage Thermal Process Produces Nanocrystalline Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.excerpt_original: The formation of nanocrystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) was investigated using boric acid and urea as starting reagents. The work focuses on the combined influence of precursor molar ratio, sequential thermal treatment, and aqueous purification on phase evolution and structural ordering. A H3BO3:(NH2)2CO ratio of 1:2 was selected from compositions of 1:1, 1:2, 1:3, and 1:4 on the basis of precursor characteristics and phase analysis. Heat treatment at 600 °C under N2, followed by 1000 °C under N2–H2, produced h-BN primary particles of 2–10 nm. The relative XRD structural-order index increased from approximately 5% after the first stage to 87% after the second stage and 98% after water washing. The findings demonstrate that precursor processability and post-treatment purification must be evaluated together with diffraction and microscopy data when developing reproducible h-BN powder technology.
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized 2–10 nm hexagonal boron nitride particles from boric acid and urea using sequential nitrogen and nitrogen–hydrogen heat treatments. Water purification further improved the X-ray diffraction structural-order index to 98%, highlighting the importance of integrating precursor control, thermal processing, and post-treatment in reproducible h-BN powder production.

articles.title_original: ULTRASOUND TREATMENT OF MODIFIED LITOL 24 LUBRICANTS
articles.title_en: Ultrasonic Treatment Improves h-BN and WS₂ Lubricant Performance
articles.excerpt_original: A comparative assessment of tribological properties of Litol 24 lubricant with the addition of 1 % hexagonal boron nitride (h BN) and 1 % tungsten disulfide (WS2), followed by ultrasonic treatment, is carried out. Microstructural analysis shows that ultrasonic cavitation promotes the breakdown of agglomerates and the homogeneous distribution of fillers in the lubricating medium. During tribological tests, it was recorded that introduction of 1% WS2 and 1% h BN, followed by ultrasonic treatment, reduces the friction force by 29–30% and 17–20%, respectively, compared to the base lubricant under a load of 40 N. At the same time, h BN shows more effective heat removal from the friction zone, which is due to its higher thermal conductivity. It is found out that WS2 is the preferred modifier for friction units operating under high loads and moderate temperatures, whereas h-BN is recommended for high temperature operating conditions. The obtained results confirm the effectiveness of ultrasonic dispersion as a method that allows the beneficial properties of nanoscale additives in plastic lubricants to be fully realized. The study objective is to evaluate the effect of ultrasonic treatment on the particle distribution pattern in the base lubricant and on the tribological properties of the resulting modified lubricants. The task the paper is devoted is to justify the choice of a modifier (WS2 or h BN) for specific operating conditions of friction units, based on the analysis of their effect on the friction force and heat generation in the friction contact zone, as well as to determine the effectiveness of ultrasonic treatment as a method for homogenizing nano additives in a highly viscous lubricating medium. The novelty of the work lies in conducting a comprehensive comparative a
articles.summary_en: Researchers evaluated Litol 24 lubricants modified with 1% hexagonal boron nitride or tungsten disulfide after ultrasonic treatment. WS₂ reduced friction by 29–30%, while h-BN provided stronger heat removal and is better suited to high-temperature applications.

articles.title_original: Electrical discharge coating of AA6062 using hBN–Cu powder metallurgy electrodes: Microstructural and tribological characteristics
articles.title_en: hBN–Cu Electrical-Discharge Coatings Improve AA6062 Tribology
articles.excerpt_original: Electrical discharge coating (EDC) is an electrothermal surface modification technique for improving the functional performance of engineering alloys. In this study, hexagonal boron nitride–copper (hBN–Cu) powder metallurgy electrodes with 70:30, 50:50 and 40:60 compositions were fabricated and used to modify AA6062 aluminum alloy. The effects of electrode composition, compaction pressure, peak current and pulse-on time on material transfer, coating thickness, surface roughness, microhardness and tribological behavior were investigated. Compaction pressure varied from 80 to 160 MPa, while peak current and pulse-on time varied from 5 to 15 A and 100 to 300 μs, respectively. The coatings were characterized using scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction and electron backscatter diffraction. Among the investigated conditions, the 50:50 hBN–Cu electrode provided the most favorable surface and tribological characteristics, with a maximum microhardness of approximately 167 HV, minimum coefficient of friction of approximately 0.19 and minimum specific wear rate of approximately 0.00160 mm 3 /N·m. Increasing compaction pressure from 80 to 160 MPa reduced Sa from 4.951 to 4.800 μm and Sz from 56.719 to 50.280 μm, while the maximum coating thickness of 32.45 μm was obtained at 120 MPa. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis indicated 87.6% Cu and 12.4% hBN, with an average misorientation of 35.64° and maximum {001} texture intensity of 3.74 MRD. These results demonstrate that controlled electrode composition and EDC parameters can improve the surface and tribological performance of AA6062.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used hBN–Cu powder-metallurgy electrodes to electrically discharge-coat AA6062 aluminum alloy. A 50:50 electrode produced the best reported performance, including approximately 167 HV microhardness, 0.19 friction coefficient and 0.00160 mm³/N·m wear rate.

articles.title_original: Reaction Energy Landscape of Propane Oxidative Dehydrogenation on Liquid Boron Oxide‐Germinated Catalytic Sites in the Presence of Dioxygen: An Orbitals‐Driven Mechanistic Study
articles.title_en: Boron Oxide Catalysts for Propane Oxidative Dehydrogenation
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Recently, boron‐based catalysts have gained significant attention for the oxidative dehydrogenation of propane into propene and ethene. In this study, we present an electronic‐level understanding of propane oxidation via a triplet dioxygen molecule over liquid boron oxide motifs, including cyclic B−O−B sites (8‐, 6‐, and 4‐membered rings) and edge B−OH and B−B sites. Our computations reveal that cyclic B−O−B and edge B−OH motifs exhibit higher activation barriers for C 3 H 6 (55–71 kcal mol −1 ) and C 2 H 4 (80–95 kcal mol −1 ) formation. In contrast, the B−B site requires the lowest barrier among all sites. Orbital analysis reveals that 3 O 2 activation at cyclic B−O−B sites proceeds via an electron transfer from O(2p) orbital into the antibonding orbitals of 3 O 2 . Over edge B−OH sites, the σ(O−H) bonding orbital facilitates 3 O 2 activation. At the B−B site, the σ(B−B) bonding orbital transfers an electron into the antibonding orbital of 3 O 2 . Furthermore, transfer of an electron from the σ(C−H) of C 3 H 8 to another antibonding orbital of 3 O 2 , leading to the generation of C 3 H 7 radical. C 2 H 4 formation over the B−B site has the lowest barrier, arising from the least strained seven‐membered ring and the simultaneous cleavage of σ(C−C) and σ(C−O) bonds. This study underscores the industrial potential of boron‐based catalysts.
articles.summary_en: Computational research maps the reaction-energy landscape of propane oxidative dehydrogenation over liquid boron oxide sites. B−B edge sites show the lowest barriers, suggesting a potentially favorable pathway for propene and ethene production, although the findings are theoretical.

articles.title_original: Recent advances in electrospun hydrogen-rich polymeric nanofiber composites for space radiation shielding
articles.title_en: Review assesses electrospun polymer nanofiber composites for space radiation shielding
articles.excerpt_original: As human space exploration extends beyond Low Earth Orbit toward sustained lunar and future Mars missions, lightweight and multifunctional radiation-shielding materials are increasingly required to mitigate the complex Galactic Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Event (SPE) environment. Hydrogen-rich polymers offer advantages over conventional high-Z metallic shields because of their low density and reduced production of high-energy secondary radiation. This review critically evaluates recent advances (2020–2026) in electrospun hydrogen-rich polymeric nanofiber composites for space radiation shielding, with emphasis on the relationships among polymer chemistry, nanofiber architecture, functional fillers, and shielding performance. Particular attention is given to polyethylene-based systems, boron-containing fillers, hierarchical architectures, and the influence of processing and interfacial characteristics on radiation attenuation and multifunctional performance. Radiation-transport modelling, including Monte Carlo approaches, together with molecular-scale and computational materials-design strategies, is examined as a route toward predictive optimization; however, limitations associated with heterogeneous datasets, model validation, and the lack of standardized mission-relevant testing remain significant barriers. The review further identifies critical challenges in electrospinning scalability, environmental durability, long-duration radiation exposure, and translation from laboratory testing to aerospace implementation. Overall, the available evidence indicates that shielding performance cannot be attributed to nanofiber morphology alone and must instead be evaluated through the combined effects of hydrogen content, areal density, architecture, filler distribution, and rad
articles.summary_en: The review examines lightweight, hydrogen-rich polymer nanofiber composites for shielding against galactic cosmic rays and solar particle events, focusing on polyethylene systems, boron fillers, architectures, and modelling. It highlights unresolved challenges in scalability, durability, standardized testing, and translating laboratory results to aerospace missions.

articles.title_original: Identifying Contact Barrier Types in Few-Layer MoS2 Devices Using Correlative IV, LBIC, and Bias-Dependent KPFM
articles.title_en: Correlative Methods Identify Contact Barriers in Few-Layer MoS₂ Devices
articles.excerpt_original: Electrical contacts between metals and two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) critically govern device performance, yet their microscopic and spatially varying contributions are difficult to disentangle with a single technique. Here we present an integrated experimental framework that combines current-voltage (IV) characterization, laser beam induced current (LBIC) mapping, and bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to correlate macroscopic transport with spatially resolved photocurrent and bias-induced potential distributions in few-layer MoS2 two-terminal devices under ambient conditions. IV measurements quantify the total resistance, its polarity dependence and the illumination response. LBIC maps the local photocurrent response with micrometer spatial resolution, separating photocurrent contributions from contact-induced electric fields and from temperature gradients. KPFM, operated under an applied static bias rather than in the conventional work-function mode, provides nanoscale-resolved potential distributions that resolve the relative bias-induced voltage drops at the contacts and in the channel. We apply this framework to three few-layer devices spanning low-resistance, asymmetric and annealing-sensitive contact regimes, one exhibiting ohmic-like and two exhibiting diode-like contact behavior and show that the combined data support a qualitative distinction between low-barrier (Ohmic-like) and contact-limited transport with Schottky-like and tunnel-like contributions and resolve the asymmetry between the two contacts. Thermal annealing strongly reduces the total resistance of a bilayer device and redistributes the voltage drop, while contact-related voltage losses remain. This correlative, readily implementable appr
articles.summary_en: Researchers combined current–voltage measurements, laser-beam-induced current mapping and bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy to distinguish ohmic-like, Schottky-like and tunnel-like contact behavior in few-layer MoS₂ devices. The approach also resolved contact asymmetry and showed that thermal annealing can reduce resistance while leaving contact-related voltage losses.

articles.title_original: Universal crystallization kinetics of solution-processed semiconductors
articles.title_en: Universal model improves crystallization control in solution-processed semiconductors
articles.excerpt_original: Heterogeneous crystallization kinetics critically govern the morphology and performance of solution-processed semiconductors, yet morphology control is often achieved through trial-and-error optimization. Quantitative understanding of crystallization is essential for precise morphology control but is limited by the simultaneous occurrence of heterogeneous nucleation and crystal growth. Here, a time-defined induced nucleation strategy has been developed to initiate crystallization at specific stages of solution processing. Systematic variation of nucleation timing reveals three distinct morphological regimes, whose emergence is explained by the concentration-dependent critical cluster radius in bulk, interfacial, and cusp environments. On this basis, a quantitative, dimensionless model is developed for heterogeneous crystallization kinetics across diverse processing conditions. The model demonstrates universality across perovskite and organic semiconductors. In situ studies reveal identical growth kinetics for induced and spontaneous nuclei, validating its generality. The resulting morphology control enables tuning of crystallinity and charge transport in solution-processed transistors.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a time-defined induced-nucleation strategy and dimensionless model to explain heterogeneous crystallization across perovskite and organic semiconductors. The approach enables morphology and charge-transport tuning in solution-processed transistors, with relevance to semiconductor applications.

articles.title_original: Towards Ideal Electron‐Transporting Transistor Characteristics in Polymer Semiconductors in Ambient Air
articles.title_en: FBDPPV Polymer Transistors Combine High Mobility with Near-Ideal Operation in Air
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The coexistence of high mobility and ideal current–voltage transistor characteristics is highly desirable for real‐work applications of field‐effect transistors. However, very few high‐mobility polymer transistors can exhibit reliability factors >70%, and even rarer for electron‐transporting devices. In this work, we report a coexistence of a reliability factor of 90% and high mobility of 0.6 cm 2 V −1 s −1 in FBDPPV‐based transistors and, more importantly, systematically investigate the origin by combining optical and microstructural characterizations and transport physics study. We found that in this rigid, coplanar, distortion‐free polymer FBDPPV, efficient charge transport that induces high mobility and near‐ideal transistor behaviors is supported by efficient intrachain transport and limited by energetic disorder along the interchain transport pathway consisting of disorderly connected very small grains. We also compare the structure‐property relationship of FBDPPV with some benchmark high‐mobility polymers and provide insights into rational design strategies for achieving the coexistence of high mobility and ideal current–voltage transistor characteristics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report FBDPPV-based polymer transistors achieving 0.6 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ mobility and a 90% reliability factor under ambient conditions. Structural and transport analyses attribute performance to efficient intrachain transport, while interchain energetic disorder remains limiting; the findings inform polymer semiconductor design.

articles.title_original: Low‐Cost, Energy‐Saving, Room‐Temperature Synthesis of Ductile Thermoelectric Semiconductors
articles.title_en: Room-Temperature Synthesis Enables Flexible Ag₂(Se,S) Thermoelectrics
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Flexible thermoelectric has recently attracted great attention in wearable technologies. Ag 2 (Se,S)‐based ductile materials are promising candidates for flexible thermoelectric applications. However, conventional melting methods with high‐temperature routes (>1000°C), which are commonly employed for the synthesis of these materials, are energy‐intensive and limited in achieving precise control over composition and homogeneity. In this work, a simple chemical reaction route was employed to synthesize Ag 2 (Se,S)‐based materials at room temperature, enabling highly homogeneous distribution and good chemical stoichiometric control. Among the S‐substituted compositions, Ag 2 Se 0.7 S 0.3 exhibited the best thermoelectric performance, and excess Ag was subsequently incorporated to regulate carrier transport. Although the Ag‐excess bulk sample achieved a zT value of 0.54 at 340 K due to reduced thermal conductivity, its power factor remained limited. Hot‐rolling deformation was therefore introduced to promote an anisotropic microstructure with grain alignment, which facilitates carrier transport and increases carrier mobility. The optimized Ag 2.05 Se 0.7 S 0.3 film achieved a maximum power factor of 13.88 µW cm −1 K −2 at 340 K. Furthermore, a six‐leg in‐plane thermoelectric device fabricated from this material delivered a normalized maximum power density of 0.44 W m − 1 under Δ T = 37.4 K, demonstrating the potential of this cost‐effective and energy‐saving room‐temperature synthesis strategy for flexible thermoelectric applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a low-cost, energy-saving room-temperature route for homogeneous, ductile Ag₂(Se,S)-based thermoelectric materials. Hot-rolled Ag₂.₀₅Se₀.₇S₀.₃ films achieved a maximum power factor of 13.88 µW cm⁻¹ K⁻² and powered a six-leg in-plane device, highlighting potential for flexible wearable thermoelectrics.

articles.title_original: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells
articles.title_en: Ordered 2D Perovskite Orientation Enables Ultrastable Solar Cells
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate‐phase film with a Ruddlesden‐Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two‐step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums‐based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm 2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1‐sun illumination (ISOS‐L‐2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a processing strategy that orders the crystallographic orientation of Dion–Jacobson 2D perovskite films by introducing a Ruddlesden–Popper phase. Resulting solar cells reached 21.1% efficiency and retained 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2,000 hours at 65°C, with 98.7% retention after 2,500 hours at 85% relative humidity.

articles.title_original: Chemical Equilibrium Modulated Crystallization of 2D Perovskite Single Crystals for High‐Performance and Robust Dual‐Mode Photonic Detection
articles.title_en: 2D Perovskite Crystals Enable Robust Dual-Mode Photonic Detection
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT 2D perovskites, characterized by distinctive quantum‐well structure and high exciton binding energy, offer unprecedented opportunities for photonic detection. However, synergistically driving efficient carrier extraction and rapid radiative recombination within monolithic single crystals (SC) remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, a room‐temperature chemical equilibrium‐modulated crystallization strategy is demonstrated to synthesize centimeter‐scale 2D (PA) 2 PbBr 4 (PPB) SCs. The use of a hygroscopic acid‐base reactive agent precisely regulates the solvent evaporation kinetics, suppressing stochastic nucleation and yielding high‐quality SCs with suppressed light scattering. Consequently, planar PPB photodetectors (PDs) exhibit a notable and robust UV response, featuring a large on/off ratio of 2.77 × 10 4 , a wide linear dynamic range of 159 dB, and an ultra‐low limit of detection of 3.5 nW cm −2 . Simultaneously, the intense exciton confinement endows the PPB SCs with strong radioluminescence and robust radiation stability. Both SCs and flexible film scintillators demonstrate excellent practical x‐ray imaging capabilities. Crucially, the absence of grain boundaries inherently mitigates internal light scattering, enabling SC scintillators to achieve an impressive spatial resolution up to 26.5 lp mm −1 , representing one of the highest values among the reported metal halide SC scintillators. This work establishes a kinetically control for high‐quality SCs synthesis and provides valuable insights for high‐performance and robust dual‐mode photonic detection.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed centimeter-scale 2D perovskite single crystals using chemical-equilibrium-modulated crystallization, achieving strong UV photodetection and radioluminescence. The crystals and flexible scintillator films supported X-ray imaging, with single-crystal scintillators reaching 26.5 lp mm−1 spatial resolution.

articles.title_original: Super-Klein tunneling in two-dimensional Lorentzian-type barriers in graphene
articles.title_en: Study predicts super-Klein tunneling in graphene barriers
articles.excerpt_original: We introduce a two-dimensional model of spin- 1 / 2 Dirac fermions in graphene subjected to a highly tunable electric field, which exhibits super-Klein tunneling. The electric field can be continuously interpolated between two limiting configurations: a uniform electrostatic Lorentzian barrier with translational invariance and a chain of well-separated electrostatic scatterers. We demonstrate that super-Klein tunneling arises naturally as a direct consequence of the intrinsic connection of the model to free-particle dynamics, a relation that is established through methods of supersymmetric quantum mechanics, which provide an elegant and analytically tractable framework. Besides the mentioned super-Klein tunneling, scale invariance of the model and invisibility of the potential for particles of specific energy are revealed, and possible routes toward experimental realization are discussed.
articles.summary_en: Researchers introduce a tunable two-dimensional model of Dirac fermions in graphene exposed to Lorentzian-type electrostatic barriers. The study derives super-Klein tunneling, scale invariance and energy-specific potential invisibility, and discusses possible experimental realization.

articles.title_original: Zener tunneling in biased bilayer graphene via analytic continuation of semiclassical theory
articles.title_en: Analytic Theory Describes Zener Tunneling in Bilayer Graphene
articles.summary_en: Researchers present an analytic-continuation approach to semiclassical theory for Zener tunneling in biased bilayer graphene. The work advances theoretical understanding relevant to graphene-based electronic and semiconductor devices, without reporting a commercial product or company involvement.

articles.title_original: Mechanochemically Controlled Functionalization of Graphene Microdrums
articles.title_en: Mechanical Strain Enables Site-Specific Functionalization of Graphene Microdrums
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Mechanochemical reactions involve the use of applied mechanical distortions to reactants to drive chemical reactions. In this work, we demonstrate the use of mechanical force to direct location-specific reactions on suspended bilayer graphene microdrums, by manipulating their geometric landscape, through the introduction of standing-wave oscillations using an atomic force microscope (AFM) probe. By introducing these oscillations into the suspended membrane while it is held in contact with an underlying reactant medium (e.g. water), the mechanically induced oxidation of graphene is observed, whereby the greatest reactivity is seen to occur at the peaks of the induced standing waves, which correspond to the regions of highest local strain in the graphene bilayers. Mapping these reactive regions using Raman microspectroscopy reveals that the radial position of the highest regions of reactivity depends on the applied oscillation frequency, beginning at the center of the microdrums at low frequencies (ca. 1–20 kHz), and then expanding outward at frequencies above 100 kHz. From finite element modeling (FEM) of the frequency-dependent mechanics of the membranes, this change in shown to be consistent with the radial redistribution of the regions of the highest local curvature of the graphene. The ability to use mechanical distortions to drive location-specific functionalization of 2D materials such as graphene provides a new route to the design of nanoscale devices and site-directed catalysis on such materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used AFM-induced standing-wave oscillations to control where oxidation occurs on suspended bilayer graphene microdrums. The strain-dependent method could support site-directed catalysis and nanoscale 2D-material devices.

articles.title_original: Scanning Probe Microscopy of Graphene Sensors Before and After Nitrogen Exposure
articles.title_en: Scanning Probe Study Reveals Nitrogen-Induced Changes in Graphene Sensors
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance, miniaturized 2D material platforms requires a deep, multiscale understanding of gas‐surface interactions and localized electronic behavior. In this study, we demonstrate an integrated experimental methodology that combines in situ environmental scanning electron microscopy (ESEM) with ex situ scanning probe microscopy (SPM) to analyze monolayer graphene field‐effect transistor (GFET) sensors before and after controlled nitrogen (N 2 ) exposure. In situ electrical measurements performed inside the ESEM chamber show a continuous, monotonic increase in graphene channel resistance (up to approximately 5%, reaching 6.30 kΩ at 160 Pa) as N 2 vapor displaces residual atmospheric contaminants. On the micro and nanoscale, ex situ SPM characterization confirms that the gross topography and structural integrity of the diagonal contact–graphene boundary remain intact post‐exposure. The initial highly heterogeneous, “charge‐puddle‐like” work‐function landscape—characterized by a low‐potential diagonal band—is replaced by a visually smoother, spatially uniform potential profile after N 2 treatment. This shift is primarily attributed to the displacement, desorption, and spatial reorganization of preadsorbed environmental p‐dopants (such as water vapor and oxygen molecules) by N 2 gas.
articles.summary_en: Researchers combined environmental electron microscopy and scanning probe microscopy to examine graphene field-effect transistor sensors before and after nitrogen exposure. Nitrogen increased channel resistance by up to approximately 5% and smoothed the work-function landscape by displacing environmental p-dopants such as water and oxygen.

articles.title_original: Metallic electron crystals in rhombohedral graphene as a bridge to twisted WSe$_2$
articles.title_en: Study links metallic Wigner crystals in rhombohedral graphene to twisted WSe₂ superconductivity
articles.excerpt_original: Superconducting phases have recently been discovered both in twisted bilayers of transition metal dichalcogenide WSe$_2$ (tWSe$_2$) and in rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG). While both have generated extensive interest, they appear to be driven by qualitatively different physics. Here, we propose a unified picture in which the superconductivity in RMG arises from a strongly correlated metallic state with a spatial length scale that is compatible with the moiré length scale of tWSe$_2$. Central to this mechanism is a Wigner crystal phase in RMG that is metallic, driven by a "W"-shaped dispersion in the flat part of the underlying graphene band structure. We demonstrate this effect through calculations of Wigner crystal states in pentalayer RMG, focusing on dilute electrons in the quarter-metal regime relevant to experiment. In a region of the phase diagram we find the Wigner crystal breaks three-fold rotation symmetry, which guides our construction of a $t$-$V$ model on a triangular lattice as an effective description of the low-energy electronic physics. This construction suggests a surprisingly similar low-energy description of RMG and tWSe$_2$. Broader implications for superconductivity in dilute carrier systems are also discussed.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose that superconductivity in rhombohedral multilayer graphene arises from a strongly correlated metallic Wigner crystal state. Their model identifies similarities between graphene and twisted WSe₂, offering a unified framework for superconductivity in dilute-carrier systems.

articles.title_original: Broadband Near-Field Imaging of Strong Polariton Coupling in Graphene/CrI3 Heterostructures
articles.title_en: Graphene–CrI3 heterostructures show strong polariton coupling
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Interfacial charge transfer in van der Waals heterostructures provides a powerful, contact-free mechanism to activate two-dimensional plasmons. Chromium iodide (CrI3), a layered ferromagnetic insulator, induces significant doping in adjacent graphene, yet its nanoscale polaritonic response and the optical manifestation of this charge transfer remain unexplored. Here, we report the direct real-space observation of propagating graphene surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) sustained entirely by spontaneous interfacial charge transfer at the graphene/CrI3 interface. Interestingly, a distinct polaritonic anticrossing near 214 cm–1 (6.4 THz) between the charge-transfer-induced graphene SPP and the CrI3 phonon is identified, suggesting this hybrid system lies within the strong-coupling regime. Our work is enabled by the recent advances in broadband synchrotron near-field nanospectroscopy and suggests intriguing opportunities for magnetically switchable polaritonics in the hybrid charge-transfer heterostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers directly observed graphene surface plasmon polaritons generated by interfacial charge transfer in graphene/CrI3 heterostructures. A polaritonic anticrossing with a CrI3 phonon indicates strong coupling and points to magnetically switchable polaritonics.

articles.title_original: Concurrent efficiency and stability gains in inverted perovskite solar cells enabled by termination-engineered MXene interfaces
articles.title_en: Termination-Engineered MXene Interfaces Improve Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.excerpt_original: Inverted perovskite solar cells are strongly affected by buried-interface losses at the hole-selective contact. Here, we report a UV–ozone-assisted surface-engineering strategy to tune the surface terminations of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene for inverted perovskite solar cells. Mild UV–ozone treatment enriches Ti–O–Ti species while reducing Ti–OH groups on the MXene surface. This termination modulation adjusts the electronic structure of Ti 3 C 2 T x , increasing its work function and narrowing the energy-level offset with the perovskite valence band at the buried hole-selective contact. The resulting Ti 3 C 2 T x /MeO-2PACz self-assembled monolayer (SAM) buried interface promotes interfacial hole extraction and suppresses nonradiative recombination, lowering the trap density. As a result, devices incorporating UV-treated Ti 3 C 2 T x achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 22.46%, compared with 19.97% for devices based on untreated Ti 3 C 2 T x . The optimized devices also show improved durability, retaining 81% and 80% of their initial efficiencies after 168 h under thermal stress and ambient storage, respectively. These results demonstrate that surface-termination engineering of MXene provides an effective route to simultaneously improve interfacial energetics, charge transport, and stability in inverted perovskite solar cells.
articles.summary_en: UV–ozone treatment of Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene enriched Ti–O–Ti terminations, improving hole extraction and reducing interfacial recombination. Resulting cells reached 22.46% efficiency versus 19.97% untreated and retained 81% and 80% of initial efficiency after thermal and ambient aging, respectively.

articles.title_original: Dual‐Functional Membranes With Interfacial MXene/PFSA Nanoarchitectures for Low Hydrogen Permeation in Water Electrolysis and Reduced Vanadium Ion Crossover in Flow Batteries
articles.title_en: MXene–PFSA Membranes Reduce Hydrogen and Vanadium Crossover
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) and vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) suffer from hydrogen and vanadium ion crossover when using conventional perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) membranes. Here we report a layer‐by‐layer MXene/PFSA membrane architecture in which MXene nanosheets are integrated into PFSA coating layers to create MXene‐regulated nanointerfaces that decouple proton conductivity from gas and ion permeation. The lamellar MXene framework introduces tortuous transport pathways and selectively perturbs PFSA hydrophilic domain organization while preserving continuous proton‐conducting networks through interfacial hydrogen bonds. As a result, the optimized membrane exhibits simultaneously enhanced H + /H 2 and H + /VO 2+ selectivity, achieving up to 43.0% lower hydrogen permeability and 37.5% reduced vanadium ion diffusion compared to pristine PFSA, without sacrificing proton conductivity. It exhibits stable long‐term operation in PEMWE with lower hydrogen and retains 67.0% capacity in VRFB over 470 cycles, outperforming pristine PFSA more than 40% of capacity retention. Small‐ and wide‐angle X‐ray scattering reveal MXene‐induced disordering and expansion of large‐scale hydrophilic domains, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the MXene/PFSA interface selectively increases transport energy barriers for hydrogen and vanadium ions while preserving low barriers for proton migration. These results validate a versatile interfacial strategy toward overcoming selectivity limitations for both PEMWE and VRFB.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed layered MXene/PFSA membranes that reduce hydrogen permeability in proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis by up to 43% and vanadium-ion diffusion in flow batteries by 37.5%, while maintaining proton conductivity. The membranes retained 67% capacity after 470 vanadium redox flow battery cycles, indicating a potentially significant selectivity improvement for energy-storage and hydrogen systems.

articles.title_original: Effect of Ti3C2Tx MXene content on the structural properties and optical band gap of PVA/PEG nanocomposite thin films
articles.title_en: MXene Loading Tunes PVA/PEG Nanocomposite Film Structure and Band Gap
articles.excerpt_original: In this work, Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene was synthesized by selective chemical etching of the Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase and incorporated into a poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/poly (ethylene glycol) (PEG) matrix to fabricate nanocomposite thin films with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene loadings of 0.5–1.5 wt% by using a simple drop-casting technique. The structural, morphological, compositional, and optical characteristics of pure PVA/PEG and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/PVA/PEG nanocomposite thin films were systematically investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and UV–Vis spectroscopy. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) analysis revealed enhanced interfacial interactions between the polymer chains and the surface functional groups of Ti 3 C 2 T x MXenes. XRD and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) results confirmed the successful formation of MXene and its incorporation into the polymer matrix. The crystallinity index showed a non-monotonic trend with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene loading, reaching a maximum at 0.5 wt% Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene with crystallinity indices of 48.01% and 49.87% as determined by XRD and FTIR, respectively, due to the heterogeneous nucleation effect of MXene nanosheets at low filler loading. UV–Vis spectroscopy showed a gradual red shift of the absorption edge as the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene concentration increased. Both the direct and indirect optical band gap energies decreased from 5.49 to 4.98 eV and from 5.17 to 3.28 eV, respectively, as the Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene content increased from 0.0 to 1.5 wt%. These findings suggest that Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/PVA/PEG nanocomposite thin films are promising candidat
articles.summary_en: Academic research shows that Ti3C2Tx MXene incorporation changes crystallinity, optical absorption, and band-gap energies in PVA/PEG nanocomposite thin films. The films reached maximum crystallinity at 0.5 wt% MXene, while higher loading progressively narrowed the optical band gap.

articles.title_original: Performance and synergistic flame-retardant mechanism of nano-hexagonal boron nitride-reinforced waterborne acrylic intumescent fire-retardant coatings
articles.title_en: Nano-Hexagonal Boron Nitride Enhances Waterborne Intumescent Fire-Retardant Coatings
articles.summary_en: The study investigates waterborne acrylic intumescent fire-retardant coatings reinforced with nano-hexagonal boron nitride. It focuses on the material’s synergistic flame-retardant mechanism and performance.

articles.title_original: Dataset for: Graphene-enhanced Thermal Interface Materials for Accelerated Quench Recovery of Superconducting Tapes in Flexible Direct Current Fault Current Limiters
articles.title_en: Dataset Quantifies Graphene Thermal Interfaces for Superconducting Fault Current Limiters
articles.excerpt_original: Underlying experimental data of the manuscript Graphene-enhanced Thermal Interface Materials for Accelerated Quench Recovery of Superconducting Tapes in Flexible Direct Current Fault Current Limiters (Xiaohong Hong, Maoming Power Supply Bureau of Guangdong Grid Co., Ltd., China). Five Excel workbooks give the numerical values plotted in Figures 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 and listed in Tables 3, 4 and 5 of the manuscript, for the graphene nanoplatelet / silicone rubber composites (SR-0, SR-G1 to SR-G8), the functionalized graphene oxide composite (SR-fGO), the hexagonal boron nitride control (SR-BN20), the epoxy-matrix control (EP-G5) and the commercial thermal-grease reference, all measured at 77 K unless stated otherwise: thermal conductivity, thermal diffusivity and specific heat with their uncertainties, quench recovery time and maximum superheat; volume resistivity, dielectric breakdown strength, relative permittivity and dielectric loss; peak quench voltage, decay time constant and initial voltage rise rate; maximum surface temperature, temperature gradient, quench-zone length and temperature-uniformity index; interfacial thermal contact resistance at 0.1 and 0.5 MPa, thermal response time, lap-shear strength, thermal-shock cycles survived (77 K / 298 K) and failure mechanism. README.md describes every file and column; file_manifest_md5.txt lists the MD5 checksum of every file. Released under CC BY 4.0.
articles.summary_en: An open dataset reports thermal, electrical, mechanical, and quench-recovery measurements for graphene nanoplatelet and functionalized graphene oxide composites at cryogenic temperatures. The data supports evaluation of graphene-enhanced thermal interface materials for flexible direct-current superconducting fault current limiters.
companies: Maoming Power Supply Bureau of Guangdong Grid Co., Ltd.

articles.title_original: Sandwich‐Structured Aramid Composite Papers with Heterogeneous Dielectric Layers for Integrated Corona Resistance and Thermal Conductivity
articles.title_en: Fluorinated Graphene–Aramid Papers Improve Thermal Conductivity and Corona Resistance
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Aramid dielectric papers are indispensable for insulation in high‐performance motors for electric vehicles, aircraft, and high‐speed rail. However, the ongoing electrification trend toward higher voltage, frequency, and power density imposes severe electrothermal stresses that conventional aramid papers cannot withstand. Their inherently low thermal conductivity leads to localized heat accumulation while poor corona resistance accelerates electrothermal aging, both compromising long‐term motor reliability. Here, we report a sandwich‐structured poly(m‐phenylene isophthalamide) (PMIA) composite dielectric paper that decouples thermal conductivity from corona resistance through a functional multilayer architecture. Fluorinated graphene (FG)/PMIA surface layers provide interface passivation and charge dissipation, while boron nitride nanotube (BNNT)/PMIA core layers enable thermal conduction and dielectric reinforcement. Electrospinning followed by hot‐pressing achieves spatially oriented functional filler arrangements. FG constructs continuous charge‐transfer barrier to suppress surface discharge and BNNT constructs continuous thermal pathways in the bulk without compromising insulation integrity. The optimized dielectric paper achieves a thermal conductivity of 10.22 W·m − 1 ·K − 1 and a corona lifetime of 147.42 min, representing 1.23‐fold and 14.7‐fold improvements over neat PMIA paper, while maintaining a high breakdown strength of 199.52 kV/mm. This specific synergy originates from hierarchically oriented architecture rather than simple property addition, offering a universal strategy to design dielectric materials with decoupled multifunctionality.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed sandwich-structured aramid dielectric papers using fluorinated graphene surface layers and boron nitride nanotube cores. The optimized material reached 10.22 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ thermal conductivity, 147.42 minutes of corona lifetime, and 199.52 kV/mm breakdown strength, indicating potential for high-voltage motor insulation.

articles.title_original: 2D Orthogonal Composition‐Gradient Perovskite Photodetection Chip for Computational Spectrometry and Imaging
articles.title_en: 2D Gradient Perovskite Chip Enables Filter-Free Computational Spectrometry
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Miniaturized computational spectrometers are highly desired for intelligent sensing and imaging, which require both a high‐spatial‐resolution photodetector array in hardware and an accurate spectral reconstruction algorithm in software. Herein, we design a space‐confined anion exchange strategy to construct continuous in‐plane composition‐gradient perovskite films along two orthogonal directions, enabling a continuously gradual shift of the bandgap across the entire visible spectrum. The resulting 2D composition‐gradient films were directly integrated with orthogonal top and bottom electrode arrays without additional material transfer to construct a compact filter‐free microspectrometer with 25 × 10 photodetection units. The device exhibits spatially variant spectral responses across the 2D plane. For the high‐dimensional response data acquired from this 2D detector array, a customized segment‐optimized adaptive reconstruction algorithm is proposed, which enables accurate spectral reconstruction with an average root‐mean‐square error of 0.0372 and a spectral resolution as low as 0.8 nm. Additionally, the device supports multispectral imaging, further highlighting its potential for integrated spectral sensing platforms. This work demonstrates a facile strategy for fabricating 2D composition‐gradient materials and offers a promising pathway toward low‐cost, integrable chip‐scale spectral sensing and imaging systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed orthogonal composition-gradient perovskite films integrated with electrode arrays to create a compact 25 × 10-unit microspectrometer. The chip achieved spectral reconstruction with 0.8 nm resolution and supported multispectral imaging, indicating potential for integrated spectral sensing and imaging.

articles.title_original: Graphene Nanoplatelet Reinforcement of Interfacial Transition Zones in Expansive Agent-Cement Composites
articles.title_en: Graphene Nanoplatelets Strengthen Cement Interfacial Zones
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Expansive agents (EAs) are widely used in concrete projects but often aggravate interfacial transition zone (ITZ) weakness due to localized expansive crystal accumulation. This study proposes the incorporation of graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) to reinforce the micromechanical and microstructural properties of the ITZ in EA-cement composites, with particular emphasis on changes in C−S−H phase assemblage, microstructural characteristics, and elemental distributions. Results showed that 0.10% GNP maximized mechanical performance, increasing total average indentation modulus and hardness by 65% and 90%, respectively, compared with the GNP-free system, while reducing ITZ thickness to 25−30 μm. ITZ porosity was reduced by 5−35%, accompanied by enhanced formation of C−S−H, portlandite, and ettringite, and an 87−90% increase in hydrated phase fraction. GNP incorporation increased the indentation modulus and hardness of loose-packed (LP), low-density (LD), and high-density (HD) C−S−H by 8−45% and redistributed phase fractions from loose-packed toward low/high C−S−H. The calculated bulk density of LP, LD, and HD C−S−H increased by 2.1−5.1%, 2.8−7.6%, and 3.6−7.8%, respectively. The local ITZ Ca/Si ratio decreased from 2.0 to 0.8−1.0, showing more polymerized, silica-rich C−S−H associated with expansive crystal regulation. This work provides a viable strategy for designing high-performance, nano-engineered, and expansive cement composites.
articles.summary_en: ACS research found that 0.10% graphene nanoplatelets improved interfacial-zone indentation modulus by 65% and hardness by 90% in expansive agent–cement composites. The reinforcement also reduced porosity and interfacial-zone thickness while promoting denser, more polymerized C–S–H formation.

articles.title_original: Diameter-Governed Vertical Growth of Graphene-Skinned Cu Wires with Enhanced Thermal Stability
articles.title_en: Vertical Graphene Coatings Improve Copper Wire Stability
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Owing to its superior electrical and thermal conductivity and low cost, copper (Cu) is essential in power, communications, and electronics. However, ongoing device miniaturization poses critical challenges to its ampacity and environmental stability. In this study, vertical graphene-skinned Cu wires of 18 μm, 500 μm, and 1 mm in diameter were prepared using a solid carbon source without additional heating. The distinct graphene morphologies on Cu wires of different diameters stemmed from their dissimilar thermal responses and the effect of exposed catalytic area on growth. The growth process and structural characteristics of vertical graphene on 18 μm Cu wires were then investigated. Compared to horizontal graphene, vertical graphene offers superior oxidation resistance. While preserving the electrical performance of the Cu wires, vertical graphene enhances their thermal stability and current-carrying capacity. This work provides a coating strategy that integrates conductivity, heat dissipation, and durability for micro-wire protection in harsh environments.
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers developed diameter-tuned vertical graphene coatings on copper wires that improve oxidation resistance, thermal stability, and current-carrying capacity without compromising electrical performance. The approach could support more durable micro-wires for power, communications, and electronics in harsh environments.

articles.title_original: Vertically Aligned Recycled Carbon Fibre/MXene Composites for Impedance‐Regulated Microwave Absorption and Thermal Management
articles.title_en: Vertically Aligned Recycled Carbon Fibre–MXene Composites Improve Microwave Absorption and Heat Transfer
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Recycled carbon fibres offer a promising sustainable route to functional composites, but their short length and disordered connectivity limit controlled electromagnetic and thermal transport. Here we use electrostatic flocking to construct vertically aligned rCF@Ti 3 C 2 T x /NiFe 2 O 4 arrays within a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix inspired by the hierarchical host–symbiont of marine sponges. The aligned architecture redistributes conductive pathways and interfacial polarization, improving impedance matching while providing through‐plane heat transport channels. Compared with the randomly dispersed composite, the vertically aligned composite at the same loading ratio deepens the minimum reflection loss (RL min ) from −33.62 to −60.71 dB. The Effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) broadens increase from 3.91 to 7.82 GHz. In thermal‐transport comparison, vertical alignment raises the through‐plane thermal conductivity from 0.18 to 4.03 W m − 1 K − 1 . These results suggest that alignment control is an effective route to upcycle short recycled fibres into multifunctional polymer composites.
articles.summary_en: Wiley researchers used electrostatic flocking to align recycled carbon fibre, MXene and nickel ferrite arrays in a polymer matrix. The architecture improved minimum reflection loss from −33.62 to −60.71 dB, widened absorption bandwidth to 7.82 GHz, and increased through-plane thermal conductivity to 4.03 W m−1 K−1.

articles.title_original: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene - Nature
articles.title_en: Gate-Controlled Layer Sliding Enables Nonvolatile Magnetic Switching in Tetralayer Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene Nature
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that an applied gate voltage can induce sliding between graphene layers, enabling nonvolatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene. The result could support research into graphene-based electronic and spintronic devices, but no commercial application is identified.

articles.title_en: Haydale Graphene Industries Listed on Yahoo Finance Canada
articles.excerpt_original: Haydale Graphene Industries (HAYD) Yahoo! Finance Canada
